**(A subtle point)**
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ (75:22–23). Thus He perfected their outward appearance with radiance, and their inner selves with gazing upon Him.

**(Another subtle point)**
If the mere sight of a created being, [Yusuf (peace be upon him)], on the day he went out before them, so overwhelmed the women's senses that they cut their hands without feeling it, then how will it be on the Day of Increase (al-Mazid)?
If you love the One worshipped, your heart will be present in His worship.

**(Section)**
Among the secrets of this surah is that Allah, glorified is He, gathered for His friends (awliya') both the beauty of the outward and the inward. He adorned their faces with radiance and their inner selves with looking upon Him. There is no greater beauty, pleasure, or sweetness for their inner selves than looking upon Him, and no greater beauty for their outward selves than the radiance of the face, which is its brightness, its embellishment, and its delight. This is like His saying in another place: ﴿And He gave them radiance and joy﴾ (76:11).

Its parallel is His saying: ﴿O Children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts, and as adornment (riyasha)﴾ (7:26). This is the beauty and adornment of the outward. Then He said: ﴿But the garment of righteousness (taqwa), that is better﴾ (7:26). This is the beauty of the inward.

Its parallel is His saying: ﴿We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars﴾ (37:6). This is the beauty of its outward. Then He said: ﴿And as a protection from every rebellious devil﴾ (37:7). This is the beauty of its inward.

Its parallel is His saying, concerning the wife of the 'Aziz after she had said to Yusuf: ﴿Go out before them.﴾ ﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him and cut their hands, and said: "Allah forbid! This is not a human. This is none but a noble angel." She said: "That is the one about whom you blamed me. I certainly sought to seduce him, but he refrained. And if he does not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned, and he will be of the debased."﴾ (12:31–32). Her mentioning him in this is part of describing his excellences, and that he was at the utmost of excellence outwardly and inwardly.

Related to this meaning, and in harmony with it, is His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is for you that you will not be hungry therein, nor will you be naked. And indeed, you will not be thirsty therein, nor will you be exposed to the sun﴾ (20:118–119). Here He contrasted hunger with nakedness, because hunger is the humiliation of the inward and nakedness is the humiliation of the outward. He also contrasted thirst, which is the heat of the inward, with exposure to the sun (ad-duha), which is the heat of the outward.

Close to this is His saying: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is taqwa﴾ (2:197), mentioning the outward sensory provision and the inward spiritual provision. The former is the provision for the journey of this world, and the latter is the provision for the journey of the Hereafter. This is connected to Hud's saying: ﴿And O my people, seek forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance; He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain and increase you in strength to your strength﴾ (11:52). The first is the outward strength, separate from them, and the second is the inward strength, joined to them.

Similar to it is His saying: ﴿So he has no strength nor any helper﴾ (86:10). Here He negated from them both the repellers: the repeller from within themselves, and the repeller from outside, which is the helper.

**(Benefit)**
In His saying: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾, it is impossible to interpret "looking" (nazar) as waiting for the reward, for He attributed the looking to the faces, which are its locus. He also made it transitive with the particle ilā (toward), which, when the verb of seeing is joined to it, means only the seeing of the eye. He described the faces with radiance, which is attained only with the presence of what is enjoyed, not with the distress of awaiting it. With this construction it is also impossible to interpret "looking" as other than sight, although "nazar" in the sense of "waiting" has been used in His saying: ﴿Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light﴾ (57:13), and His saying: ﴿And I will wait (nathira) with what the messengers will return﴾ (27:35).

He also said in *al-Sawa'iq al-Mursala*: Similar to this is the consistent manner of the texts regarding looking at Allah: "Thus you will see your Lord, and you will look upon your Lord," and ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾. It has never come in a single place "you will see the reward of your Lord," so that what departs from its counterparts would be interpreted in that way.

**[Section: The perfection of pleasure is in the perfection of the Beloved and the perfection of love]**
This is a great matter which the intelligent person must attend to: that the perfection of pleasure, joy, delight, the bliss of the heart, and the gladness of the spirit follows two matters. The first is the perfection of the Beloved in Himself and in His beauty, and that He is most deserving of having love directed to Him above everything else. The second matter is the perfection of one's love, the exhausting of one's effort in loving Him, and preferring nearness to Him and reaching Him above all things.

Every intelligent person knows that the pleasure of attaining the Beloved is in proportion to the strength of one's love. Whenever love is stronger, the lover's pleasure is more complete. So the servant's pleasure is in proportion to the intensity of his thirst upon attaining cool water, or the intensity of his hunger upon eating delicious food, and similar things, according to the measure of his longing and the intensity of his will and love.

Once you know this, pleasure, delight, and joy are matters sought in themselves; indeed they are the aim of every living and intelligent being. When pleasure is sought for its own sake, it is blamed if it results in a greater pain, or if it prevents a better and more lasting pleasure. How much more so if it results in the greatest regrets and causes the loss of the greatest delights and joys? It is praised when it helps toward a great, lasting, firmly established pleasure, in which there is no distress or turbidity in any way, and that is the pleasure of the Hereafter, its bliss, and the goodness of life therein. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ (87:16–17).

When the sorcerers said to Pharaoh after they had believed: ﴿So decide what you will decide. You can only decide concerning this worldly life. Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and the magic you compelled us to practice. And Allah is better and more enduring﴾ (20:72–73).

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, created the creation so that He might bestow upon them this lasting pleasure in the abode of eternity. As for this world, it is cut off, and its pleasures never become pure nor do they endure. This is unlike the Hereafter, whose pleasures are lasting, and whose bliss is pure of every turbidity and pain. In it is what the souls desire and what the eyes delight in, along with eternity forever. ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes﴾ (32:17). Rather, in it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human.

This is the meaning intended by the sincere advisor to his people: ﴿O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the path of right conduct. O my people, indeed this worldly life is but enjoyment, and indeed the Hereafter is the abode of permanence﴾ (40:38–39). He informed them that this world is enjoyed as a means to something else, and that the Hereafter is the place of settling.

Once you know that the pleasures and bliss of this world are an enjoyment and a means to the pleasures of the Hereafter, and that for this reason this world and its pleasures were created, then every pleasure that helped toward the pleasure of the Hereafter and led to it is not blamed for being taken. Rather, it is praised according to the extent to which it leads to the pleasure of the Hereafter.

Once this is known, the greatest bliss and pleasures of the Hereafter are: looking upon the Face of the Lord, may His majesty be exalted; hearing His speech directly from Him; and nearness to Him. As is established in the Sahih in the hadith of the vision: "By Allah, He has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking upon Him." And in another hadith: "When He manifests Himself to them and they see Him, they forget what they are in of bliss."

In the Sunan of al-Nasa'i and the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) in his supplication: "And I ask You, O Allah, for the delight of looking upon Your Noble Face, and the longing for meeting You." In *Kitab al-Sunnah* of 'Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad, marfu' (traced to the Prophet): "It is as if people on the Day of Resurrection had never heard the Qur'an, when they hear it from the Most Merciful, as if they had not heard it before that."

**[Section: That the delight of looking upon the Face of Allah on the Day of Resurrection follows the enjoyment of knowing and loving Him in this world]**
Just as there is no comparison between the bliss of anything in Paradise and the bliss of looking upon the Face of the Most High, glorified is He, so there is no comparison between the bliss of this world and the bliss of loving Him, knowing Him, longing for Him, and being intimate with Him. Rather, the delight of looking upon Him, glorified is He, follows their knowledge of Him and their love for Him, for pleasure follows perception and love. Thus, whenever the lover is more knowing of the Beloved and more intense in love for Him, his delight in His nearness, his vision, and his arrival to Him will be greater.

**(Section)**
Hisham ibn Hassan said, from al-Hasan (al-Basri): When the people of Paradise look upon Allah, Exalted is He, they forget the bliss of Paradise.

Hisham ibn 'Ammar said: Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Sabur narrated to us; 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman narrated to us; Sa'id ibn 'Abd Allah al-Jarshi al-Qadi narrated to us, that he heard Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani narrate from al-Harith al-A'war, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, traced to the Prophet, who said:

"When Allah has settled the people of Paradise in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire, He will send to the people of Paradise the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibril), who will say: 'O people of Paradise, indeed your Lord sends you His greetings and commands you to visit Him at the courtyard of Paradise, which is its open plain (abtah), whose soil is musk, whose pebbles are pearls and rubies, whose trees are of gold with fresh fruit, and whose leaves are emerald.' So the people of Paradise go forth joyful and glad. Then He gathers them there, and there is the honor of Allah and the looking upon His Face, which is the promise of Allah that He has fulfilled for them. Allah then permits them to listen, eat, and drink, and they are clothed in garments of honor. Then a caller calls: 'O friends of Allah, has there remained anything of what Allah your Lord promised you?' They say: 'No. We have received what was promised to us, and nothing remains except looking upon His Face.' Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, manifests Himself to them behind veils and says: 'O Jibril, raise My veil for My servants, that they may look upon My Face.'

He said: So the first veil is raised, and they look upon a light from the light of the Lord, and they fall down prostrate before Him. The Lord calls to them: 'O My servants, raise your heads, for this is not an abode of works; it is only an abode of reward.' Then the second veil is raised, and they look upon something even greater and more majestic, so they fall prostrate in praise of Allah. The Lord calls to them: 'Raise your heads, for this is not an abode of works; it is only an abode of reward and lasting bliss.' Then the third veil is raised, and at that moment they look upon the Face of the Lord of the worlds. They say, when they look upon His Face: 'Glory be to You; we have not worshipped You with the worship You deserve.'

Then He says: 'My honor has enabled you to look upon My Face and has made you dwell in My abode.' Allah then permits Paradise to speak, and it says: 'Blessed is the one who dwells in me, blessed is the one who lives forever in me, blessed is the one for whom I have been prepared.' This is His saying: ﴿Blessed are they, and a good return﴾ (13:29), and His saying: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾."

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There are two gardens of gold, their vessels and ornaments and what is in them; and two gardens of silver, their vessels and ornaments and what is in them. Nothing stands between the people and looking upon their Lord except the cloak of greatness over His Face in the Garden of Eden."

'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi narrated: Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us; Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ka'b (al-Ahbar), who said: Allah has never looked upon Paradise except that He said: "Be good for your people," and it increased in goodness beyond what it was. And there is no day that was a festival in this world except that they go out, in its measure, to the gardens of Paradise, and the Lord, blessed and exalted, manifests Himself to them and they look upon Him, and the wind blows upon them with perfume and musk. They ask their Lord, blessed and exalted, for nothing except that He gives it to them. Then they return to their families, having increased in beauty and goodliness seventy times over what they had been.

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Shababah informed me, from Isra'il, who narrated to us, from Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks upon his servants, his bliss, and his couches for a distance of a thousand years; and the most honored of them before Allah is the one who looks upon His Face morning and evening." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾. Related by al-Tirmidhi in his *Jami'*, from him.

'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi narrated from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When the people of Paradise reach the fullest extent of bliss and think there is no bliss greater than it, the Lord, blessed and exalted, manifests Himself to them, and they look upon the Face of the Most Merciful, and they forget every bliss they had witnessed when they looked upon the Face of the Most Merciful."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding His saying: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾: "Allah has beautified them by looking upon Him, glorified is He, and it is rightful for them to be radiant while looking upon their Lord, Mighty and Majestic."

Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: "If the people of love, or he said the people of knowledge (ma'rifah), had nothing but this verse, ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾, it would suffice them."

al-Nasa'i mentioned, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Do you suffer any difficulty in seeing the sun on a day with no clouds, and the moon on a full-moon night with no haze?" We said: "No." He said: "Indeed you will see your Lord, until one of you will be brought near to Him, and He will say: 'My servant, do you recognize such-and-such a sin?' He will say: 'O Lord, did You not forgive me?' He will say: 'By My forgiveness you have reached this.'"

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, says to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise!' They say: 'At your service, our Lord, and at your pleasure, and all good is in Your hands.' He says: 'Are you content?' They say: 'And why would we not be content, when You have given us what You have not given anyone of Your creation?' He says: 'Shall I not give you something better than that?' They say: 'O Lord, and what is better than that?' He says: 'I shall let My pleasure descend upon you, and I shall never be displeased with you after this.'"

In the Sahih, the Sunan, and the Masanid, from the hadith of Thabit al-Bunani, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, a caller calls: 'O people of Paradise! Indeed you have a promise with Allah, which He wishes to fulfill for you.' They say: 'What is it? Has He not whitened our faces, made heavy our scales, admitted us to Paradise, and saved us from the Fire?' Then the veil is lifted, and they look upon Him. By Allah, Allah has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking upon Him, nor anything more pleasing to their eyes."

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: "Indeed you will see your Lord as you see this moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in performing the prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so."

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Ata' ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that people said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you have any difficulty seeing the moon on the night of the full moon?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Do you have any difficulty seeing the sun when there is no cloud between us and it?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Indeed you will see Him in the same way." And in another wording: "Indeed you will not be harmed in seeing your Lord except as you are harmed in seeing them both."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 75, verses 22–23 (part 2 of 7):

Al-Tirmidhi said: Qutaybah narrated to us: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection in one plain. Then the Lord of the worlds, blessed and exalted, will look down upon them and say: 'Let every person follow what he used to worship.' So the one who worshipped the cross will be given his cross, the one who worshipped images will be given his images, and the one who worshipped the fire will be given his fire, and they will follow what they used to worship. The Muslims will remain, and the Lord of the worlds, blessed and exalted, will look down upon them and say: 'Will you not follow the people?' They will say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from You, we seek refuge in Allah from You. Allah is our Lord. This is our place until we see our Lord.' And He will command them and make them firm. Then He will withdraw, and then He will look down upon them again and say: 'Will you not follow the people?' They will say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from You, we seek refuge in Allah from You. Allah is our Lord, and this is our place until we see our Lord.' And He will command them and make them firm." They said: "Will we see Him, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Do you have any difficulty seeing the moon on the night of the full moon?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Then you will have no difficulty seeing Him at that hour." He said: "Then He will withdraw, and then He will look down and make Himself known to them, and then He will say: 'I am your Lord, so follow Me.' The Muslims will stand up, and the Ṣirāṭ (bridge) will be set up, and they will cross over it like the swiftest horses and riders, and their saying on it will be: 'Safety, safety!' The people of the Fire will remain, and a group of them will be cast into it. It will be said: 'Are you full?' and it will say: 'Is there more?' Then another group will be cast into it, and it will be said: 'Are you full?' and it will say: 'Is there more?' until, when they have been fully filled, the Most Merciful, blessed and exalted, will place His foot in it, and it will draw in upon itself, and say: 'Qaṭ, qaṭ (Enough, enough).' Then when Allah has admitted the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of the Fire into the Fire, Death will be brought in a form (mulabbiyan) and stopped on the wall between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. Then it will be said: 'O people of Paradise!' and they will look up in fear. Then it will be said: 'O people of the Fire!' and they will look up rejoicing, hoping for intercession. It will be said to the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire: 'Do you recognize this?' They will say: 'Yes, both of us recognize it. It is Death, which was assigned to us.' Then it will be laid down and slaughtered at the wall. Then it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, eternal life with no death! O people of the Fire, eternal life with no death!'"

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hadith ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ (good and sound). Its origin is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim), but this wording is more comprehensive and more concise. In the wording of al-Tirmidhi: "If anyone were to die from joy, the people of Paradise would die, and if anyone were to die from grief, the people of the Fire would die."

In the Musnad of al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Usāmah, from the narration of Qurrah, from Mālik, from Ziyād ibn Saʿd, who said: Abū al-Zubayr narrated to us, saying: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh (may Allah be pleased with both of them) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the nations will be gathered, and every people will be called with their leader. We will come last among the people, and someone among the people will say: 'Is this from this Ummah?' Then the people will look towards us, and it will be said: 'This is the trustworthy nation, this is the Ummah of Muhammad, and this is Muhammad among his Ummah.' Then a caller will call out: 'You are the last and the first.' So we will come and step over the necks of the people until we are the closest of the people to Allah, the Exalted, in station. Then the people will be called, each people with their leader. The Jews will be called, and it will be said: 'Who are you?' They will say: 'We are the Jews.' It will be said: 'Who is your prophet?' They will say: 'Our prophet is Mūsā (Moses).' It will be said: 'What is your book?' They will say: 'Our book is the Torah.' It will be said: 'What do you worship?' They will say: 'We worship ʿUzayr and we worship Allah.' He will say to those around Him: 'Lead them into Hell.' Then the Christians will be called, and it will be said: 'Who are you?' They will say: 'We are the Christians.' It will be said: 'Who is your prophet?' They will say: 'Our prophet is ʿĪsā (Jesus).' It will be said: 'What is your book?' They will say: 'Our book is the Gospel.' It will be said: 'What do you worship?' They will say: 'We worship ʿĪsā and his mother, and Allah.' He will say to those around Him: 'Lead these into Hell.' Then ʿĪsā will be called, and He will say to ʿĪsā: 'O ʿĪsā, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?' He will say: 'Glory be to You, it is not for me to say what I have no right to say,' up to His words ﴿the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾.

Then every people will be called with what they used to worship. Then a crier will cry out: 'O people, whoever used to worship a god, let him follow it.' Their gods will go before them, some of them wood and stones, some the sun and the moon, and some the Dajjāl (Antichrist), until only the Muslims remain. He will stand over them and say: 'Who are you?' They will say: 'We are the Muslims.' He said: 'The best name and the best call.' He will say: 'Who is your prophet?' They will say: 'Muhammad.' He will say: 'What is your book?' They will say: 'The Qur'ān.' He will say: 'What do you worship?' They will say: 'We worship Allah alone, with no partner.' He said: 'That will benefit you, if you are sincere.' They said: 'This is our day that we were promised.' He will say: 'Do you know Allah when you see Him?' They will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'And how do you know Him when you have not seen Him?' They will say: 'We know that there is none like Him.' He said: 'Then He will reveal Himself to them, blessed and exalted, and they will say: "You are our Lord, blessed are Your names," and they will prostrate to Him. Then the light will pass on with its people."

In the Musnad of Imam Aḥmad (may Allah be pleased with him), from the narration of Abū al-Zubayr, who said: I asked Jābir about the approach (al-wurūd), and he informed me that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "We will come on the Day of Resurrection to a mound above the people, and the nations will be called with their idols and what they used to worship, the first and then the next. Then our Lord will come to us after that and say: 'What are you waiting for?' They will say: 'We are waiting for our Lord.' He will say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'Until we look at You.' Then He will reveal Himself to them, laughing, and they will follow Him."

ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī mentioned that Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā al-Ashʿarī came to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and said: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will gather the nations on the Day of Resurrection in one plain. When He wishes to separate His creation, He will make a likeness for every people of what they used to worship, and they will follow them until they cast them into the Fire. Then our Lord will come to us while we are in a place, and He will say: 'Who are you?' We will say: 'We are the believers.' He will say: 'What are you waiting for?' We will say: 'We are waiting for our Lord.' He will say: 'How do you know that He is your Lord?' We will say: 'The messengers told us, or the books came to us.' He will say: 'Do you know Him?' They will say: 'We know that there is none like Him.' Then He will reveal Himself to us laughing, and He will say: 'Rejoice, O Muslims, for there is not one of you but that a Jew or a Christian has been put in his place in the Fire.'"

ʿUmar said to Abū Burdah: "By Allah, did you hear Abū Mūsā narrate this hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, besides whom there is no god, I heard my father mention it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) more than once, not twice or three times." ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: "I have not heard in Islam a hadith more beloved to me than this one."

In al-Tirmidhi, from the narration of al-Awzāʿī, who said: Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyyah narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, that he met Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), and Abū Hurayrah said: "I ask Allah, exalted, to gather me and you in the market of Paradise." Saʿīd said: "Is there a market in it?" He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed me that when the people of Paradise enter it, they will descend according to the merit of their deeds. They will be permitted to stay for a period equal to a Friday of worldly days, and they will visit Allah, blessed and exalted. His Throne will be displayed to them, and He will manifest Himself to them in a garden of the gardens of Paradise. Pulpits of light, pulpits of pearls, pulpits of ruby, pulpits of chrysolite, pulpits of gold and pulpits of silver will be set up for them. The lowest of them, and there is no one lowly among them, will sit on mounds of musk and camphor. They will not think that those on the chairs are superior to them in station."

Abū Hurayrah said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?'" He said: "Yes. Do you have any difficulty seeing the sun and the moon on the night of the full moon?" We said: "No." He said: "Likewise, you will have no difficulty seeing your Lord. No one in that assembly will remain but that Allah will address him directly, until He says to a man among them: 'O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, do you remember the day when you did such and such?' And He will remind him of some of his betrayals in the world. He will say: 'O Lord, did You not forgive me?' He will say: 'Yes. By the vastness of My forgiveness you have reached this station.' While they are in that state, a cloud will overshadow them from above and rain upon them a perfume the like of which they have never smelled. Then He will say: 'Arise to what I have prepared for you of honor, and take what you desire.' We will come to a market surrounded by the angels, containing what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has conceived. Whatever we desire will be brought to us. Nothing there is sold or bought. In that market the people of Paradise will meet one another. A man of high rank will come and meet one lower than himself, and there is no one lowly among them, and he will be startled by what he sees of his clothing. Before he finishes his speech, something better than it will be displayed upon him, for it is not fitting that anyone grieve there. Then we will return to our dwellings, and our wives will meet us and say: 'Welcome and well come! You have come, and your beauty and fragrance are greater than when you left us.' He will say: 'We sat today with our Lord, the Almighty, and it befits us to return with the like of what we have returned with.'"

Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said in his Musnad: Ibn al-Muṣaffā narrated to us, Suwayd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Khālid narrated to us, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise will visit the Lord, blessed and exalted, every Friday," and he mentioned what they will be given. He said: "Then Allah, exalted, will say: 'Remove the veils.' They will remove one veil after another until He reveals Himself to them from His face, blessed and exalted, as though they had never received a blessing before that. This is the saying of Allah, exalted: ﴿And with Us is more﴾."

ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī mentioned, from the hadith of al-Ḥasan (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a mursal (a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain): "Our Lord will come to us on the Day of Resurrection while we are on a high place, and He will reveal Himself to us laughing." A sound mursal.

ʿUthmān al-Dārimī said: Abū Mūsā narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, al-Ajlaḥ narrated to us, al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim narrated to us, who said: "Allah will command the heaven on the Day of Resurrection, and it will split open with those in it, and they will surround the earth and those upon it. Then He will command the second heaven," until he mentioned the seven heavens, and they will be seven ranks surrounding the people. Then the Highest King, majestic in His splendor and beauty, will descend with what He wills of the angels.

ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd said: Hishām ibn Khālid al-Dimashqī narrated to us, and he was trustworthy, Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb ibn Shāwar narrated to us, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh, mawlā (client) of Ghufrah, narrated to us, from Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibrīl came to me with a mirror in his palm, in which there was a black spot. I said: 'What is this, O Jibrīl?' He said: 'This is Friday, which your Lord sent to you, so that it may be a guidance for you and your Ummah after you.' I said: 'And what do we have in it?' He said: 'For you there is much good in it. You are the last and the first on the Day of Resurrection. In it there is an hour that no believing servant will meet while praying and asking Allah for good, which is decreed for him, but He will grant it to him; and no good that is not decreed for him, but He will store for him something better than it; and no servant seeks refuge in Allah from what is written for him, but He will ward off from him something greater than it.' I said: 'What is this black spot?' He said: 'This is the hour of the day the Resurrection will come, and it is the lord of the days, and we call it among ourselves the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazīd).' I said: 'Why do you call it the Day of Increase, O Jibrīl?' He said: 'Because your Lord has taken in Paradise a wide valley of white musk. When it is Friday from the days of the Hereafter, the Mighty descends from His Throne to His chair, to that valley, and the chair is surrounded by pulpits of light on which the truthful and the martyrs will sit on the Day of Resurrection. Then the people of the chambers will come until they surround the mound. Then the Lord of majesty and honor, blessed and exalted, will appear to them and say: "I am the One who was truthful to you in My promise, who completed My blessing upon you, and who settled you in the abode of My honor. Ask Me." They will all say: "We ask You for Your pleasure with us." He will bear witness to them of His pleasure. Then He will say: "Ask Me," and they will ask Him until the desire of every servant is fulfilled. Then He will say: "Ask," and they will say: "Our Lord is sufficient for us, we are pleased." Then the Mighty, majestic in His majesty, will return to His Throne, and there will be opened for them, according to the brightness they have on Friday, what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. The people of the chambers will return to their chambers, which are of white pearl, red ruby and green emerald, without fracture or flaw, with rivers flowing beneath them and their fruits hanging low, with their wives, their servants and their dwellings. They will never be more in need of a day than of the Day of Friday, so that they may increase in grace from their Lord and in His good pleasure.'"

This was narrated from Anas by a group, among them ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmayr ibn al-Yaqẓān, and through him al-Shāfiʿī narrated it in his Musnad, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Imām Aḥmad in al-Sunnah. Among them are Abū Ṣāliḥ, al-Zubayr ibn ʿAdī, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam al-Bunānī, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, Yazīd al-Raqqāshī, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayd, all from Anas. A group of the memorizers (ḥuffāẓ) declared it ṣaḥīḥ. Al-Shāfiʿī added at its end in his Musnad: "And this is the day on which your Lord settled on the Throne." ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah transmitted it through several routes, and in some of them he said: "Then their Lord, blessed and exalted, will reveal Himself to them and say: 'I am the One who was truthful to you in My promise, who completed My blessing upon you, and this is the place of My honor,'" up to his saying: "Then He will rise upon His chair, and the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs will rise with Him, and the people of the chambers will return to their chambers."

Muḥammad ibn al-Zabarqān narrated, from Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise will indeed need the scholars in Paradise as they needed them in this world, because they will visit their Lord every Friday. He will say to them: 'Wish.' They will say: 'What shall we wish, when You have admitted us to Paradise and given us what You have given us?' It will be said to them: 'Wish,' and they will turn to the scholars." He mentioned the hadith about the story of Friday.

Ibn Mandah narrated, from the hadith of al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ḥudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), the full story of Friday, in which he says: "Ask Me. They will say: 'Show us Your face, Lord of the worlds, that we may look at You.' Then Allah, blessed and exalted, will remove those veils, and He will reveal Himself to them, and they will look at Him."

ʿUthmān al-Dārimī mentioned, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, that he related to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz: "When Allah has finished with the people of Paradise and the Fire, He will approach in shades of clouds with the angels, and He will greet the people of Paradise at the first rank, and they will return His greeting."

Al-Quraẓī said: "And this is in the Qur'ān: ﴿Peace, a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾."

Then He will say: "Ask Me," and He will do this with them in their ranks, until He settles upon His Throne. Then gifts from Allah will come to them, carried by the angels to them.

ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd narrated, from al-Ḥasan: "If the worshippers knew that they would not see their Lord in the Hereafter, their souls would melt away in this world."

Hishām ibn Ḥassān narrated from him: "He, blessed and exalted, will reveal Himself to the people of Paradise, and when they see Him, they will forget the blessings of Paradise."

(Chapter: On their seeing their Lord, blessed and exalted, with their eyes openly, as the moon is seen on the night of the full moon, and His manifesting Himself to them smiling.)

This chapter is the most noble of the chapters of this book, the most exalted in rank, the most delightful to the eyes of the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jamāʿah, the followers of the Prophet's way and the united body of believers), and the most grievous to the People of Innovation (ahl al-bidʿah) and misguidance. It is the goal toward which the diligent strive, the object of the competitors' rivalry, and the race of the racers. For the like of it let the workers work. When the people of Paradise attain it, they forget what they are in of bliss; and its deprivation and the veil from it for the people of Hell is harder for them than the torment of Hell. The prophets and messengers, all the Companions, the Successors, and the leaders of Islam agreed upon it across the successive generations. Its deniers are the apostate innovators, the Jahmiyyah (followers of Jahm ibn Ṣafwān, who denied divine attributes), the Pharaonic deniers who strip Allah of His attributes (muʿaṭṭilah), the Bāṭiniyyah (esoteric sects who rejected the outward meaning of religion) who have stepped out of all religions, and the Rāfiḍah (Rafidites, the extreme Shiites) who cling to the snares of Satan and are cut off from the rope of Allah. They are engaged in reviling the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, they wage war on the Sunnah and its people, and they are at peace with every enemy of Allah, His Messenger, and His religion. All of these are veiled from their Lord and driven away from His door. They are the factions of misguidance, the followers of the accursed one, and the enemies of the Messenger and his party.

Allah, glorified and exalted, has informed us about the one among creation most knowledgeable of Him in his time, namely His interlocutor (kalīm), His confidant (najī), and His chosen one (ṣafī) from among the people of the earth, that he asked his Lord, exalted, to look upon Him. His Lord, blessed and exalted, said to him: ﴿You will not see Me, but look at the mountain. If it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me. But when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust﴾.

The indication of this verse is from several aspects.

The first: it is not to be supposed of the interlocutor of the Most Merciful, and His noble messenger, that he would ask his Lord for what is impermissible for Him, indeed for what is among the most manifest falsehood and the greatest impossibility. This is, according to the philosophers of the Greeks, the Sabians, and the Pharaonic deniers, like asking Him to eat, drink, sleep, and the like, from which Allah is exalted. So, how strange it is that the followers of the Sabians, the Magians, and the idolatrous idol-worshippers, and the offshoots of the Jahmiyyah and the Pharaonic deniers, have become more knowledgeable about Allah, exalted, than Mūsā ibn ʿImrān (Moses son of ʿImrān), and about what is impossible for Him and what is necessary for Him, and more emphatic in declaring Him transcendent than he was.

The second aspect: Allah, glorified and exalted, did not reject his request. Had it been impossible, He would have rejected it from him. For this reason, when Ibrāhīm the Friend (al-Khalīl) asked his Lord, blessed and exalted, to show him how He gives life to the dead, He did not reject it from him. When ʿĪsā ibn Maryam asked his Lord to send down a table from heaven, He did not reject his request. But when Nūḥ asked his Lord for the salvation of his son, He rejected his request and said: ﴿I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾. He said: ﴿My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers﴾.

**The third aspect:** He answered him with His words ﴿You will not see Me﴾. He did not say "Do not see Me," nor "I am not seen," nor "My sight is not permissible." The difference between these answers is clear to anyone who reflects on them. This indicates that He, may He be glorified and exalted, can be seen, but Musa's faculties could not bear seeing Him in this world, because human strength in this world is too weak to see Him, exalted is He. The following explains this.

**The fourth aspect** is His words ﴿But look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me﴾. Thereby He informed him that the mountain, despite its strength and solidity, cannot endure His manifestation to it in this world. How then could weak humans, who were created from weakness, endure it?

**The fifth aspect:** Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, is able to make the mountain remain firm in its place. This is not impossible within His power; rather it is possible. He has made seeing Him conditional upon it. Had seeing Him been impossible in its essence, He would not have made it conditional upon something possible in itself. And had seeing been impossible, it would be like someone saying: "If the mountain remains firm, I will eat, drink and sleep." By your own reckoning, both matters would be equal.

**The sixth aspect** is His words, exalted is He, ﴿And when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust﴾. This is one of the clearest proofs that it is permissible for Him, blessed and exalted is He, to be seen. For if it is permissible for Him to manifest Himself to the mountain, which is an inanimate object with no reward or punishment, how could it be impossible for Him to manifest Himself to His prophets, messengers and friends in the abode of their honour, and show them Himself?

Thus He, may He be glorified and exalted, informed Musa that if the mountain could not remain firm when faced with His sight in this world, then humans are even weaker.

**The seventh aspect:** His Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, spoke to him directly, addressed him, conversed with him and called to him. Whoever is permitted to speak and to be spoken to, and whose addressee can hear his speech directly without an intermediary, then seeing Him is even more deserving of being permitted. For this reason, denying the vision cannot be complete except by denying the speaking. These sects combined the denial of both matters: they denied that anyone speaks to anyone or that anyone sees anyone. Therefore Musa, peace be upon him, asked to look at Him, and He made him hear His speech. The Prophet of Allah knew that seeing Him was permissible from the fact that his Lord had spoken to him and addressed him. He did not inform him that it was impossible for Him to be seen; rather He showed him that what he asked for, he could not bear, just as the mountain could not remain firm at His manifestation.

As for His words, exalted is He, ﴿You will not see Me﴾, they indicate negation in the future only, and do not indicate perpetual negation, even if it is restricted by "never." How much less so when it is unrestricted! Allah, exalted is He, says ﴿And they will never wish for it﴾, alongside His words ﴿And they will call: "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!"﴾.

**Section: The second proof** is His words ﴿And fear Allah, and know that you will meet Him﴾; His words ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be "Peace"﴾; His words ﴿Those who are certain that they will meet Allah said﴾; and His words ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾. The people of the language agree that when "meeting" (liqa') is attributed to a living being with sound sight and no impediment, it necessarily implies direct witnessing and seeing. This is not invalidated by His words ﴿So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him﴾. For the clear and authentic hadiths indicate that the hypocrites will see Him in the plains of Resurrection, and so too will the disbelievers, as in the two Sahihs, in the hadith of the manifestation on the Day of Resurrection, which will pass before you shortly, Allah willing. On this question there are three opinions among the people of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah, the adherents of orthodox tradition):

1. Only the believers will see Him.
2. All the people of the place of standing see Him, believers and disbelievers alike; then He veils Himself from the disbelievers, and they never see Him after that.
3. The hypocrites see Him, but the disbelievers do not.

All three opinions are found in the school of Ahmad, and his followers held all three. The same three opinions also apply to His speaking to them. Our Shaykh (Ibn Taymiyyah) wrote a separate impartial work on this, in which he related the three opinions and the arguments of their proponents.

Likewise is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O man, you are labouring towards your Lord with toil, and you will meet Him﴾. If the pronoun refers to the deed, then the meaning is its being seen written and recorded. If it refers to the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, then it is the meeting with Him that was promised.

**The third proof** is His words ﴿And Allah calls to the abode of peace, and guides whom He wills to a straight path. For those who did good is the best reward, and more. Neither dust nor humiliation will cover their faces. Those are the companions of Paradise; therein they will abide forever﴾.

So "the best reward" is Paradise, and "more" is the sight of His noble face. This is how the Messenger of Allah, who received the Qur'an, explained it, and then the Companions after him. As Muslim related in his Sahih, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾ and said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, a herald will call out: 'O people of Paradise, you have a promise from Allah, and He wishes to fulfil it for you.' They will say: 'What is it? Has He not made our scales heavy, whitened our faces, admitted us to Paradise and saved us from the Fire?' Then the veil will be lifted, and they will look upon Allah. Nothing He has given them is dearer to them than looking at Him. This is the 'more'."

Al-Hasan ibn Arafah said: Muslim ibn Salim al-Balkhi told us, from Nuh ibn Abi Maryam, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about this verse, ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾. He said: "For those who did good in this world, the best reward is Paradise, and the 'more' is looking at the face of Allah, exalted is He."

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, from Ka'b ibn Ujrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His words, exalted is He, ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾: "The 'more' is looking at the face of the Most Merciful, majestic is His majesty." I said to Ata: "This is al-Khurasani, not Ata ibn Abi Rabah."

Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn Abd al-Rahim told us, from Amr ibn Abi Salamah, who said: I heard Zuhayr ibn Muhammad say: "Someone who heard Abu al-Aliyah al-Riyahi narrate told me..." Ya'qub ibn Sufyan said: Safwan ibn Salih told us, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, who said: someone who heard Abu al-Aliyah al-Riyahi narrate told me, from Abu Ka'b, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the "more" in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, His words ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾. He said: "The best reward is Paradise, and the 'more' is looking at the face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

Abu al-Sunnah (Asad al-Sunnah) said: Qays ibn al-Rabi' told us, from Aban, from Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi, that he heard Abu Musa narrate that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "On the Day of Resurrection, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will send a herald who will call out: 'O people of Paradise!' with a voice that the first and last of them will hear: 'Allah has promised you the best reward, and the best reward is Paradise, and the "more" is looking at the face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'"

Ibn Wahb said: Shabib told me, from Aban, from Ibn Tamimah al-Hujaymi, that he heard Abu Musa al-Ash'ari narrate from the Messenger of Allah that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commands a herald on the Day of Resurrection to call out: "O people of Paradise! Allah has promised you the best reward and more. The best reward is Paradise, and the 'more' is looking at the face of the Most Merciful."

As for the Companions: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Yasar told us, from Abd al-Rahman, that is Ibn Mahdi, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾, that he said: "The 'more' is looking at the noble face of Allah." By the same chain, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim ibn Yazid, from Hudhayfah, concerning ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾, he said: "The 'more' is looking at the face of their Lord, exalted is He."

Ali ibn Isa told us, from Shababah, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: I heard Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi narrate from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, exalted is He, will send a herald to the people of Paradise, who will call out: 'Has Allah fulfilled His promise to you?' They will look at what Allah has prepared for them of honour, and they will say: 'Yes.' Then He will say to those who did good: 'The best reward and more: looking at the face of the Most Merciful, the Mighty and Majestic.'"

Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali: Abu Tamimah informed us, saying: I heard Abu Musa al-Ash'ari giving a sermon to the people in the congregational mosque of Basra, saying: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah sends an angel to the people of Paradise who says: 'O people of Paradise, has Allah fulfilled His promise to you?' They look and see the ornaments, the garments, the rivers and the pure spouses, and they say: 'Yes, Allah has fulfilled His promise to us.' Then the angel says, three times: 'Has Allah fulfilled His promise to you?' They do not deny anything of what was promised, and they say: 'Yes.' Then he says: 'There is still something left for you: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to those who did good, the best reward and more.' The best reward is Paradise, and the 'more' is looking at the face of Allah, exalted is He."

In the Tafsir of Asbat ibn Nasr, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Malik and Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas; and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, concerning ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more; neither dust nor humiliation will cover their faces﴾: "As for the best reward, it is Paradise; as for the 'more', it is looking at the face of Allah, exalted is He; and as for dust, it is blackness."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, Amir ibn Sa'd, Isma'il ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Suddi, al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, Qatadah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid ibn Jabr all said: "The best reward is Paradise, and the 'more' is looking at the face of Allah, exalted is He."

Many of the early scholars (salaf) said concerning the verse ﴿neither dust nor humiliation will cover their faces﴾ that it means after looking at Him. The reports from them to this effect are authentic.

Since He, may He be glorified and exalted, joined the "more" by conjunction to the "best reward", which is Paradise, this indicates that it is a different matter beyond Paradise and an additional quantity over it. As for whoever interprets the "more" as forgiveness and good pleasure (ridwan), that is among the necessary consequences of seeing the Lord, blessed and exalted is He.

**Section.** **The fourth proof** is His words, exalted is He: ﴿No! Indeed, on that Day they will be veiled from their Lord﴾.

The argument from it is that He, may He be glorified and exalted, made being veiled from His sight and from hearing His speech among the greatest punishments of the disbelievers. So if the believers did not see Him and did not hear His speech, they too would be veiled from Him. This argument was also used by al-Shafi'i himself and by other imams. Al-Tabarani and others related from al-Muzani, who said: I heard al-Shafi'i say concerning His words, exalted is He, ﴿No! Indeed, on that Day they will be veiled from their Lord﴾: "In it is evidence that the friends of Allah will see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Hakim said: al-Asamm told us, from al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, who said: I was present with Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i when a note came to him from Egypt asking: "What do you say concerning the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿No! Indeed, on that Day they will be veiled from their Lord﴾?"

Al-Shafi'i said: "Since these were veiled in wrath, this is evidence that His friends will see Him in good pleasure."

Al-Rabi' said: I said, "O Abu Abd Allah, do you say this?" He said: "Yes, and I am religiously bound to it. Had Muhammad ibn Idris not been certain that he would see Allah, he would not have worshipped Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

Al-Tabarani related it in Sharh al-Sunnah through the chain of al-Asamm as well. Abu Zur'ah al-Razi said: I heard Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn say: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Hakam was asked whether all creatures, believers and disbelievers, would see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah said: "None will see Him except the believers." He said: "Al-Shafi'i was also asked about the vision, and he said: Allah says, ﴿No! Indeed, on that Day they will be veiled from their Lord﴾. In this is evidence that the believers are not veiled from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

**Section: The fifth proof** is the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿For them is whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more﴾.

Al-Tabarani said: Ali ibn Abi Talib and Anas ibn Malik said that the "more" is looking at the face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Zayd ibn Wahb and others among the Successors (tabi'un) said the same.

**Section: The sixth proof** is the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Not perceived by eyes, but He perceives the eyes﴾. The argument from this is the most surprising of all, since it is one of the proofs of those who deny the vision. Yet our Shaykh set out the argument from it in the finest and most subtle manner. He said to me: "I commit myself to the principle that no misguided person can cite a verse or a sound hadith in support of his falsehood without there being in that same evidence something that indicates the opposite of his claim. Among such verses is this one, and it is more indicative of the permissibility of the vision than of its impossibility. Allah, exalted is He, mentioned it in the context of praise. It is well known that praise is only for attributes of affirmation (thubutiyyah). Pure non-existence is not perfection and is not praised. The Lord, blessed and exalted is He, is praised by negation only when that negation implies a positive existential attribute. Examples include His praise by negating drowsiness and sleep, which implies the perfection of self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah); negating death, which implies the perfection of life; negating weariness and fatigue, which implies perfect power; negating a partner, a consort, a child and a helper, which implies the perfection of His lordship, dominion and subjugation; negating eating and drinking, which implies the perfection of self-sufficiency (samadiyyah) and His independence; negating intercession with Him without His permission, which implies the perfection of His oneness and His independence from His creation; negating injustice, which implies the perfection of His justice, knowledge and independence; and negating forgetfulness and anything being absent from His knowledge, which implies the perfection of His knowledge and comprehensiveness; and negating likeness, which implies the perfection of His essence and attributes.

For this reason He did not praise Himself with a pure negation that implies no positive attribute, because the non-existent shares with the existent that negation. The Perfect One is not described by something He shares with the non-existent. If the meaning of ﴿not perceived by eyes﴾ were that He cannot be seen in any way, there would be no praise or perfection in it, since the non-existent shares that with Him. Pure non-existence is not seen and is not perceived by eyes, and the Lord, majestic is His majesty, is exalted above being praised by something He shares with pure non-existence. Therefore the meaning is that He is seen, but not perceived, and not encompassed. This is like the meaning of His words ﴿Nor is absent from your Lord the weight of an atom﴾, that He knows everything; and His words ﴿And no fatigue touched Us﴾, that He is perfect in power; and His words ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾, that He is perfectly just; and His words ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾, that He is perfectly self-subsisting.

So His words ﴿Not perceived by eyes﴾ indicate the utmost of His greatness, that He is greater than everything, and that because of His greatness He is not perceived in such a way that He is encompassed. For perceiving (idrak) is encompassing a thing, and it is an additional quality beyond seeing, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿When the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said: 'We are surely overtaken!' He said: 'No!'﴾"

Therefore, the sight of God is not negated for Moses, and the people did not mean by their saying "Indeed, we are overtaken" (inna lamudrakun) that "we are seen" (inna lamar'iyyun). Moses, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, negated their overtaking him with his saying "No!" (kalla). God, glorified and exalted, also informed that he would not fear their overtaking him, in His saying: ﴿And We revealed to Moses: Travel by night with My servants, and strike for them a dry path through the sea, not fearing to be overtaken, nor afraid﴾. Sight (ru'yah) and overtaking (idrak) each may exist with the other and without it. The Lord, exalted is He, is seen and not overtaken, as He is known and not encompassed. This is what the Companions and the Imams understood from the verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The eyes do not perceive Him" means the eyes do not encompass Him. Qatadah said: "He is greater than that the eyes could perceive Him." 'Atiyyah said: "They look at God, but their eyes do not encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them." This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Eyes do not perceive Him, but He perceives the eyes﴾.

So the believers will see their Lord, blessed and exalted is He, with their eyes, plainly, and their eyes will not overtake Him, meaning that they will not encompass Him, since it is impermissible to describe God, mighty and majestic, as being encompassed by anything, while He is encompassing all things. Likewise, He hears the speech of whomever He wills of His creation, and they do not encompass His speech. Likewise, He knows what He has taught the creation, and they do not encompass His knowledge.

Similar to this is their argument for negating the attributes by His saying: ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾. This is among the greatest proofs of the abundance of His attributes of perfection and the descriptions of His majesty. Because of their abundance, greatness and vastness, He has no likeness in them. Otherwise, if by it were meant the negation of attributes, then pure non-existence would be more deserving of this praise than Him. Moreover, all rational people understand from a speaker's saying "So-and-so has no equal, no peer, no like" that he is distinguished from people by attributes and descriptions that they do not share with him. The more his attributes and descriptions increase, the more his like is absent and he is distanced from resembling his peers. Thus His saying ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾ is among the strongest indications of the abundance of His descriptions and attributes. His saying ﴿Eyes do not perceive Him﴾ is among the strongest indications that He is seen and not overtaken. His saying: ﴿He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne. He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ is among the strongest indications of the Lord's distinction from His creation. He did not create them within His essence, but created them outside His essence, then He separated Himself from them by His establishment upon His Throne, while He knows what they are upon. He sees them, His sight penetrates them, and He encompasses them in knowledge, power, will, hearing and sight. This is the meaning of His being with them wherever they are. Contemplate the beauty of this correspondence in wording and meaning, and between it and His saying: ﴿Eyes do not perceive Him, but He perceives the eyes﴾.

For He, in His greatness, is exalted above being perceived by eyes or encompassed by them, and in His subtlety and awareness He perceives the eyes, so nothing is hidden from Him. He is the Great in His subtlety, the Subtle in His greatness, the Exalted in His nearness, the Near in His exaltedness, "there is nothing like Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing." ﴿Eyes do not perceive Him, but He perceives the eyes, and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted﴾.

**Section: The Seventh Proof**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord﴾.

If you remove this verse from its distortion, from its displacement from its proper places, and from lying against the Speaker, glorified is He, regarding what He intended by it, you will find it proclaiming clearly that God, glorified is He, is seen with the eyes on the Day of Resurrection. If you refuse except to distort it, which the distorters call ta'wil (figurative interpretation), then the ta'wil of the texts concerning the Return, Paradise, Hellfire, the Balance and the Reckoning is easier for their advocates than the ta'wil of this verse, and likewise the ta'wil of every text the Qur'an and the Sunnah contain. No deviant on the face of the earth seeks to interpret the texts and distort them from their proper places except that he finds a way to do so, as the one who interprets such texts found. This is what has corrupted religion and worldly life.

The attachment of looking (nazar) to the face, which is its place in this verse, and its being transitive with the particle "ila" (to), which is explicit in visual sight, and the absence from the speech of any indicator showing that the intended meaning of the looking attached to the face and transitive with "ila" is contrary to its literal sense and proper usage, is explicit that God, glorified and exalted, intended by it the sight of the eye that is in the face, directed at the Essence of the Lord, majestic is He. For looking has several usages according to its connection and its transitivity. If it is transitive by itself, its meaning is waiting and expecting, as in His saying: ﴿Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light﴾. If it is transitive with "fi" (in), its meaning is reflection and consideration, as in His saying: ﴿Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾. If it is transitive with "ila" (to), its meaning is beholding with the eyes, as in His saying: ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit﴾. So how much more so when it is attached to the face, which is the place of sight?

Yazid ibn Harun said: Mubarak informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: "I looked at my Lord, blessed and exalted is He, and I looked with His light." Now, O Sunni, listen to the interpretation of this verse by the Prophet (ﷺ), his Companions, the Successors (tabi'un) and the Imams of Islam. Ibn Mardawayh said in his tafsir: "Ibrahim narrated to us, from Muhammad, Salih ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Yazid ibn al-Haytham narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, al-Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Thuwayr ibn Abi Najiyah, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾, 'From brightness and beauty,' ﴿looking at their Lord﴾, 'He said: at the face of Allah, mighty and majestic.'" Abu Salih narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿looking at their Lord﴾: "They look at the face of their Lord, mighty and majestic." 'Ikrimah said concerning ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾: "From bliss," and ﴿looking at their Lord﴾: "They look at their Lord with a look." Then he related the like of this from Ibn 'Abbas. This is the saying of every exegete from the People of the Sunnah and Hadith.

As for the hadiths from the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions indicating the vision (of God), they are mutawatir (widely transmitted). They were narrated from him by Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Jarir ibn 'Abdullah al-Bajali, Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud al-Hudhali, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, 'Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i, Anas ibn Malik al-Ansari, Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami, Abu Razin al-'Uqayli, Jabir ibn 'Abdullah al-Ansari, Abu Umamah al-Bahili, Zayd ibn Thabit, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, 'A'ishah the Mother of the Believers, 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, 'Imarah ibn Ruwaybah, Salman al-Farisi, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As (and his hadith is mawquf, stopping at the Companion), Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd (and his hadith is mawquf), and a man from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who was not named. Here is the sequence of their hadiths from the Sahih collections, the Musnads and the Sunan. Receive them with acceptance, submission and an open heart, not with distortion and alteration, nor with narrowness of spirit. Do not deny them, for whoever denies them will not be among those looking at the face of his Lord, and will be among those veiled from Him on the Day of Resurrection.
