As for the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl al-Mazini narrated to me, saying: Abu Na'amah narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Unaydah al-Bara' ibn Nawfal narrated to me, from Dalan al-'Adawi, from Hudhayfah, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rose one day, prayed the dawn prayer, and sat until it was forenoon. The Messenger laughed, then sat in his place until he prayed the noon, afternoon and evening prayers, not speaking throughout all that, until he prayed the final night prayer (isha), then went to his family. The people said to Abu Bakr: 'Will you not ask the Messenger of Allah what is his state? He has done today something he never did before.' So he asked him, and he said: 'Yes. There was presented to me what will happen concerning the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. The first and the last were gathered in one open plain, and people were overwhelmed by that until they went to Adam, with the sweat and the distress choking them. They said: "O Adam, you are the father of mankind, and Allah, mighty and majestic, chose you. Intercede for us with your Lord." He said: "I have encountered what you have encountered. Go to your father after your father, to Noah," ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of 'Imran over the worlds﴾.' He said: 'They go to Noah, peace be upon him, and say: "Intercede for us with your Lord, for Allah chose you, and answered your supplication, and did not leave upon the earth any dwelling of the disbelievers." He says: "That is not with me. Go to Abraham, for Allah took him as a close friend (khalil)." They go to Abraham, and he says: "That is not with me. Go to Moses, for Allah, mighty and majestic, spoke to him directly." Moses says: "That is not with me. Go to 'Isa ibn Maryam, for he healed the blind and the leper and gave life to the dead." 'Isa says: "That is not with me. Go to the master of the children of Adam. Go to Muhammad, let him intercede for you with your Lord." He said: 'He goes and comes to Jibril, his Lord blessed and exalted is He. Allah, mighty and majestic, says to him: "Permit him, and give him the good news of Paradise." So Jibril takes him, and he falls in prostration for the duration of a Friday (jumu'ah). Allah, mighty and majestic, says: "Raise your head, speak, you will be heard, and intercede, you will be granted intercession." He raises his head, and when he looks at the face of his Lord, he falls prostrate again for the duration of another Friday. Allah, mighty and majestic, says: "Raise your head, speak, you will be heard, and intercede, you will be granted intercession." He goes to fall prostrate, and Jibril takes him by the arms, and Allah opens upon him of supplication something He never opened upon any human before. He says: "O my Lord, You created me the master of the children of Adam, and I say so without boasting, and I am the first from whom the earth is split open on the Day of Resurrection, without boasting, until he will be given to drink at the Pool more than the distance between San'a and Ayla." Then it is said: "Call the truthful (siddiqin)," and they intercede. Then it is said: "Call the prophets," and the prophet comes with his community (al-'usabah), and the prophet with five or six, and the prophet with no one. Then it is said: "Call the martyrs," and they intercede for whomever they wish. When the martyrs have done that, Allah, mighty and majestic, says: "I am the Most Merciful of the merciful. Enter My Paradise whoever did not associate anything with Me." They enter Paradise. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, says: "Look among the people of the Fire; do you find anyone who ever did any good?" They find in the Fire a man, and they say to him: "Did you ever do any good?" He says: "No, except that I used to be lenient with people in trade." Allah, mighty and majestic, says: "Be lenient with My servant for his leniency toward My servants." Then they bring out from the Fire another man, and say to him: "Did you ever do any good?" He says: "No, except that I instructed my children: when I die, burn me in fire, then grind me until I am like kohl, then take me to the sea and scatter me in the wind. By Allah, the Lord of the worlds will never be able to seize me ever." Allah, mighty and majestic, says to him: "Why did you do that?" He says: "Out of fear of You." Allah, mighty and majestic, says: "Look at a kingdom, the greatest kingdom, for you have its like and ten times its like." He says: "Do you mock me while You are the King?" That is what made him laugh, the forenoon laughter.'

**Section**

As for the hadiths of Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, that some people said: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you suffer any harm in seeing the moon on the night of the full moon?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Do you suffer any harm in seeing the sun when there is no cloud in front of it?" They said: "No." He said: "Indeed, you will see Him in the same way. Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection and say: Whoever used to worship anything, let him follow it. So whoever used to worship the sun follows the sun, whoever used to worship the moon follows the moon, and whoever used to worship the false gods (taghut) follows the false gods. This community remains, with its hypocrites. Allah, exalted is He, comes to them in a form other than the form they recognize and says: 'I am your Lord.' They say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from You. This is our place until our Lord comes to us. When our Lord comes, we will recognize Him.' Then Allah, mighty and majestic, comes to them in the form they recognize and says: 'I am your Lord.' They say: 'You are our Lord,' and they follow Him. The Sirat is set up between the back of Hell, and I and my community will be the first to cross it. No one speaks that day except the messengers, and the call of the messengers that day is: O Allah, grant safety, grant safety. In Hell are hooks like the thorns of the sa'dan plant. Have you seen the sa'dan?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "They are like the thorns of the sa'dan, except that no one knows the measure of their size but Allah, mighty and majestic. They snatch people according to their deeds: some are destroyed by their deeds, and some are held back until they are saved. When Allah has finished judging among the servants and wants to bring out by His mercy whomever He wills of the people of the Fire, He commands the angels to bring out of the Fire those who did not associate anything with Allah, whom Allah wills to have mercy on, those who say: 'There is no god but Allah.' They recognize them by the mark of prostration. The Fire consumes the son of Adam except the mark of prostration, for Allah forbade the Fire to consume the mark of prostration. They come out of the Fire, having been burned, and the water of life is poured over them, and they sprout as a seed sprouts in the flood-carried silt. Then Allah finishes judging among the servants, and there remains a man facing the Fire, who is the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise. He says: 'O my Lord, turn my face away from the Fire, for its wind has scorched me and its flame has burned me.' He supplicates to Allah as long as Allah wills. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, says: 'Would you perhaps, if I do that, ask for anything else?' He says: 'No, I will not ask You for anything else.' He gives his Lord covenants and pledges as Allah wills. So Allah turns his face away from the Fire. When he faces Paradise and sees it, he remains silent as long as Allah wills, then says: 'O my Lord, bring me forward to the gate of Paradise.' Allah says: 'Did you not give Your covenants and pledges that you would not ask Me for anything but what I gave you? Woe to you, son of Adam, how treacherous you are!' He says: 'O my Lord,' and supplicates to Allah until He says to him: 'Would you perhaps, if I give you that, ask Me for anything else?' He says: 'No, by Your might,' and gives his Lord whatever covenants and pledges He wills. So Allah brings him forward to the gate of Paradise. When he stands at the gate of Paradise, Paradise opens up for him, and he sees what is in it of good and joy. He remains silent as long as Allah wills, then says: 'O my Lord, admit me into Paradise.' Allah, blessed and exalted, says to him: 'Did you not give Your covenants and pledges that you would not ask Me for anything but what I gave you? Woe to you, son of Adam, how treacherous you are!' He says: 'O my Lord, let me not be the most wretched of Your creation.' He keeps supplicating to Allah until Allah laughs at him. When Allah laughs at him, He says: 'Enter Paradise.' When he enters it, Allah says to him: 'Wish.' He asks his Lord and wishes until Allah reminds him: 'Wish for such and such,' until his wishes are exhausted. Allah, mighty and majestic, says: 'That is yours, and the like of it with it.'" Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: "And ten times its like with it." 'Ata' ibn Yazid said: "Abu Sa'id al-Khudri was with Abu Hurayrah and did not contradict any of his narration until Abu Hurayrah narrated." Abu Hurayrah said: "Allah, mighty and majestic, said to that man, 'That is yours and the like of it with it.'" Abu Sa'id said: "And ten times its like with it, O Abu Hurayrah." Abu Hurayrah said: "I only memorized His saying, 'That is yours and the like of it with it.'" Abu Sa'id said: "I testify that I memorized from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) His saying, 'That is yours and ten times its like.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "That man is the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 75, verses 22–23 (part 5 of 7):

It is also related in the Two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, the two authentic collections of Bukhari and Muslim) from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that some people in the time of the Messenger of Allah said: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes. Do you have any difficulty in seeing the sun at midday when the sky is clear and there are no clouds? And do you have any difficulty in seeing the moon on the night of the full moon when the sky is clear and there are no clouds?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: "You will not have any difficulty in seeing your Lord, Blessed and Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection, except as you have difficulty in seeing either of them. When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out that every nation should follow what it used to worship. So no one who used to worship other than Allah, whether idols or stone altars, will remain, but they will all fall into the Fire. Then, when none remain except those who used to worship Allah, both the righteous and the wicked, and the remnants of the People of the Book, the Jews will be called and it will be said to them: 'What did you used to worship?' They will say: 'We used to worship Uzair, the son of Allah.' It will be said: 'You have lied. Allah did not take a consort or a son. So what do you seek?' They will say: 'O our Lord, we are thirsty, so give us water.' They will be pointed to and told: 'Will you not come forward?' Then they will be gathered toward the Fire, which will appear like a mirage, its parts crushing one another, and they will fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be called and it will be said to them: 'What did you used to worship?' They will say: 'We used to worship the Messiah, the son of Allah.' It will be said to them: 'You have lied. Allah did not take a consort or a son.' It will be said to them: 'What do you seek?' They will say: 'O our Lord, we are thirsty, so give us water.' He said: They will be pointed to and told: 'Will you not come forward?' Then they will be gathered toward Jahannam, which will appear like a mirage, its parts crushing one another, and they will fall into the Fire. Then, when none remain except those who used to worship Allah, both the righteous and the wicked, the Lord of the Worlds, Glorified and Exalted, will come to them in the lowest of the forms in which they saw Him. He will say: 'What are you waiting for? Let every nation follow what it used to worship.' They will say: 'O our Lord, we parted from the people in this world when we were most in need of them, and we did not keep their company.' He will say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from You. We do not associate anything with Allah,' two or three times, until some of them nearly turn back. He will say: 'Is there between you and Him a sign by which you recognize Him?' They will say: 'Yes.' Then the Shin will be uncovered, and no one who used to prostrate to Allah of his own accord will remain except that Allah will permit him to prostrate. And no one who used to prostrate out of fear or for show will remain except that Allah will make his back one solid piece, so that whenever he tries to prostrate he will fall on his back. Then they will raise their heads, and He will have changed into the form in which they saw Him the first time. He will say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'You are our Lord.' Then the Bridge will be laid over Jahannam, and intercession will be granted." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), what is the Bridge?" He said: "A slippery place, with hooks, claws and a thorny barb, like the thorny plant called sa'dan that grows in Najd. The believers will cross over like the blink of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like birds, and like the finest horses and riding camels. Some will be saved intact, some will be scratched and released, and some will be thrown into the Fire of Jahannam. When the believers have been delivered from the Fire, by Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you is more insistent in demanding his right from Allah, the Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection, than the believers are on behalf of their brothers who are in the Fire. They will say: 'Our Lord, they used to fast with us, pray with us and perform Hajj.' It will be said to them: 'Bring out those whom you recognize.' Their forms will be forbidden to the Fire, and they will bring out a great number of people whom the Fire had taken up to the middle of their shins and their knees. They will say: 'Our Lord, no one remains in it of those You commanded us to bring out.' He will say: 'Return. Whoever you find in his heart a weight of half a dinar of good, bring him out.' They will bring out a great number. Then they will say: 'Our Lord, we did not leave in it anyone of those You commanded us.' Then He will say: 'Return. Whoever you find in his heart a weight of an atom's weight of good, bring him out.' They will bring out a great number. Then they will say: 'Our Lord, we did not leave in it anyone of those You commanded us.' Then He will say: 'Return. Whoever you find in his heart a weight of half a dinar of good, bring him out.' They will bring out a great number. Then they will say: 'Our Lord, we did not leave in it anyone of those You commanded us.' Then He will say: 'Return. Whoever you find in his heart a weight of an atom's weight of good, bring him out.' They will bring out a great number. Then they will say: 'Our Lord, we did not leave in it any good at all.'" Abu Sa'id al-Khudri used to say: "If you do not believe me about this hadith, then recite, if you wish: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾."
Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say: "The angels have interceded, the Prophets (ﷺ) have interceded, and the believers have interceded, and only the Most Merciful of the Merciful remains." He will take a handful from the Fire and bring out a people who never did any good. They will have become charred, and He will cast them into a river at the mouths of Paradise called the River of Life. They will come out like a seed grows in the sediment of a flood. Do you not see how it grows beside a stone or a tree, and that the part that faces the sun is yellow and green, while the part that faces the shade is white? They said: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it is as if you had been pasturing in the desert." He said: "They will come out like pearls, with seals on their necks. The people of Paradise will recognize them, and the people of Paradise will say: 'These are the freed ones of Allah, whom Allah has admitted into Paradise without any deed they did or any good they sent ahead.' Then He will say: 'Enter Paradise, and whatever you see is yours.' They will say: 'Our Lord, You have given us what You have not given anyone among the worlds.' He will say: 'I have something better than this for you.' They will say: 'O our Lord, what could be better than this?' He, Exalted, will say: 'My pleasure. I will never be displeased with you after this, ever.'"

As for the hadith of Suhayb, Muslim related it in his Sahih from the narration of Hammad ibn Salama, from Thabit, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'Do you want anything more that I should give you?' This is a hadith that the imams related from Hammad and received from their Prophet (ﷺ) with acceptance and confirmation.

As for the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, al-Tabarani said: "Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Azdi, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal and al-Hadrami told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ubayd ibn Abi Karima al-Harrani told us, Muhammad ibn Salama al-Harrani told us, from Abu Abd al-Rahim, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abu Ubayda ibn Abdullah, from Masruq ibn al-Ajda', who said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud told us from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: 'Allah will gather the first and the last for an appointed day, standing for forty years, their eyes fixed on the sky, waiting for the judgment to be pronounced.' He said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will descend in shadows of clouds from the Throne to the Kursi. Then a caller will call out: O people, are you not content with your Lord, who created you, provided for you, and commanded you to worship Him and not associate anything with Him? Is it not just from your Lord that each of you be given what he used to take as his ally and worship in this world?' They will say: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then every people will go to what they used to worship and take as allies in the world.' He said: 'They will set out, and forms resembling what they used to worship will be presented to them. Some of them will go to the sun, some to the moon, some to the idols of stone and to things resembling what they used to worship.' He said: 'For those who used to worship Jesus, a devil in the form of Jesus will be presented, and for those who used to worship Uzair, a devil in the form of Uzair will be presented. Muhammad and his community will remain, and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will come to them and say: What is wrong with you that you do not set out as the people have set out? They will say: Indeed we have a God whom we have not seen since. He will say: Would you recognize Him if you saw Him? They will say: Between us and Him there is a sign, and when we see it we will recognize Him. He will say: What is it? They will say: He will uncover His shin. At that moment He will uncover His shin, and they will fall down prostrate before Him. But there will remain a people whose backs are like the horns of cattle, who want to prostrate but cannot, though they used to be called to prostrate while they were sound. Then He will say: Raise your heads. They will raise their heads, and He will give them their light according to their deeds. Some of them will be given light the size of a great mountain, walking before them. Some will be given light smaller than that, and some will be given light like a palm tree in their right hand. Some will be given light smaller than that, until the last of them, a man, will be given light on the big toe of his foot, which will flash once and go out once. When it flashes he will advance and walk, and when it goes out he will stop. The Lord, Blessed and Exalted, will be before them until He passes into the Fire, leaving a trace like the edge of a sword.' He said: 'He will say: Pass on. They will pass according to their light. Some will pass like the blink of an eye, some like lightning, some like clouds, some like a falling star, some like the wind, some like a galloping horse, and some like a riding camel, until the one whose light was on the size of his big toe crawls on his face, his hands and his feet. His hands will be dragged, one hand will hang, his feet will be dragged, one foot will hang, and the sides of his body will be struck by the Fire. He will keep going like this until he is saved. When he is saved, he will stand upon it and say: All praise is for Allah, who has given me what He has not given anyone, since He saved me from it after I had seen it.' He said: 'He will be taken to a pool at the gate of Paradise, where he will wash himself, and the fragrance and colours of the people of Paradise will return to him. He will see what is in Paradise through the gate, and he will say: My Lord, admit me into Paradise. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say to him: Would you ask for Paradise after I have saved you from the Fire? He will say: O my Lord, put a barrier between me and it, so that I do not hear its sound. He said: Then he will enter Paradise. He said: A dwelling will appear to him, or be raised up before him, as if what he is in were a dream, so that he may enter it. He will say: My Lord, give me that dwelling. He will say: Perhaps if I give it to you, you will ask for something else. He will say: No, by Your might, I will ask for nothing else. And what dwelling could be better than it? He said: So it will be given to him, and he will settle in it. He said: Then another dwelling will appear or be raised before him, further ahead than that, as if what he is in were a dream, so that he may enter it. He will say: My Lord, give me that dwelling. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: Perhaps if I give it to you, you will ask for something else. He will say: No, by Your might, I will ask You for nothing else. And what dwelling could be better than it? He said: So it will be given to him, and he will settle in it. Then he will be silent, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: What is wrong with you that you do not ask? He will say: My Lord, I have asked You until I am ashamed before You, and I have sworn to You until I am ashamed before You. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: Are you not content that I give you the like of the world since the day I created it until the day I bring it to an end, and ten times that? He will say: Do you mock me while You are the Lord of Might? He said: Then the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, laughed at his words.' He said: 'I saw Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, whenever he reached this point in this hadith, laugh. A man said to him: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, I have heard you narrate this hadith many times, and every time you reach this point you laugh. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrate this hadith many times, and every time he reached this point in the hadith he laughed, until his molars showed. He said: The Lord of Might, Mighty and Majestic, will say: No, but I am able to do that. Ask. He will say: Let me join the people. He will say: Go and join the people. He said: So he will go running in Paradise, until when he approaches the people a palace of pearl will be raised for him, and he will fall prostrate. It will be said to him: Raise your head, what is wrong with you? He will say: I saw my Lord, or my Lord appeared to me. It will be said to him: It is only one of your dwellings. He said: Then he will meet a man, and he will prepare himself to prostrate. It will be said to him: Stop, what is wrong with you? He will say: I thought you were an angel. He will say: I am only a keeper of your treasuries, a servant of yours under my authority are a thousand guards like me. He said: So he will walk ahead of him until the palace is opened for him. He said: It is of hollow pearl, its roofs, doors, locks and keys are of it. A green jewel will meet him, lined with red, each jewel leading to another jewel of a different colour from the other. In each jewel there is joy, spouses and maidservants, the least of whom is a dark-eyed houri, wearing seventy garments, whose leg marrow can be seen through her garments. Her liver is a mirror for him and his liver is a mirror for her. If he turns away from her, she turns away, and she becomes seventy times more beautiful in his eyes than she was before. He will say to her: By Allah, you have become seventy times more beautiful in my eyes. She will say to him: By Allah, and you too have become seventy times more beautiful in my eyes. It will be said to him: Look up. He will look up, and it will be said to him: Your kingdom extends a hundred years' journey, as far as his sight can reach.' He said: 'Umar said: Do you not hear what Ibn Umm Abd is telling us, O Ka'b, about the least of the people of Paradise in rank, and what about the highest? Ka'b said: O Commander of the Faithful, in it is what no eye has seen and no ear has heard: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made a dwelling in which is whatever He wills of spouses, fruits and drinks, then He has sealed it, so that none of His creation has seen it, neither Gabriel nor any other angel.' Then Ka'b recited: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾."

He said: "And He created below that two gardens, adorned them with what He willed, and showed them to whomever He willed of His creation." Then He said: ﴿And for whoever feared the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ Then He said: ﴿Whoever's record is in 'Illiyyun,﴾ and ﴿He will enter that abode which no one has seen, until a man from the people of 'Illiyyun goes out and walks through his kingdom, and no tent of the tents of Paradise remains but that the light of his face enters it. They rejoice in his fragrance and say: "How sweet is this fragrance! This is a man from the people of 'Illiyyun, who has gone out walking through his kingdom."﴾ He said: "Woe to you, O Ka'b! These hearts have become heedless, so restrain them." Ka'b said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, on the Day of Resurrection Hell will have a roaring sigh, and no angel brought near nor prophet sent will remain but that he will fall to his knees, until Abraham, the Friend of Allah, says: 'My Lord, myself, myself!' Even if you had the deeds of seventy prophets added to yours, you would think you would not be saved."

This is a great hadith, sound (hasan), narrated by the compilers of the Sunnah such as Abdullah ibn Ahmad, al-Tabarani, and al-Daraqutni in the book al-Ru'yah. He related it from Ibn Sa'id: "Muhammad ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, Warqa' ibn Umar narrated to us, Abu Tayyibah narrated to us, from Karz ibn Wabarah, from Nu'aym ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah." He also related it through Abd al-Salam ibn Harb: "al-Dallani narrated to us, al-Minhal ibn Amr narrated to us, from Abu Ubaydah, with the same." He related it through Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abu Ubaydah, with the same. And he related it through Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyibah, from Karz ibn Wabarah, from Nu'aym ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Ubaydah.

**Section**

As for the Successors (tabi'un), the early Muslims, and the company of faith among the imams of hadith, jurisprudence, tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis), and Sufism, their statements are too many to be encompassed except by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: "The increase (ziyadah) is looking at the face of Allah." Malik narrated it from Yahya, from him. Al-Hasan said: "The increase is looking at the face of Allah," narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from him. Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla said: "The increase is looking at the face of Allah, the Exalted," narrated by Hammad ibn Zayd from Thabit, from him. Amir ibn Sa'd al-Bajali said it; Sufyan related it from Abu Ishaq, from him. Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit said it, narrated by Jarir ibn al-Layth from him. Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and Ka'b said it.

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote to one of his governors: "To proceed: I enjoin you to fear Allah, to adhere to His obedience, to hold fast to His command, and to keep the covenant concerning what Allah has entrusted you with of His religion and made you guardian of His Book. By the fear of Allah the friends of Allah were saved from His wrath, by it they accompanied His prophets, by it their faces were made radiant and they looked upon their Creator. It is a safeguard in this world from trials and from the distress of the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Hasan said: "If the worshippers in this world knew that they would not see their Lord in the Hereafter, their souls would melt in this world." Al-A'mash and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The most noble of the people of Paradise are those who look upon Allah, Blessed and Exalted, morning and evening." Ka'b said: "Allah, Exalted, has never looked upon Paradise except that He said: 'Be good, O Paradise, for your people,' and it increased sevenfold over what it was, until its people come to it. There is no day that was a festival for them in this world but that they go out for its duration into the gardens of Paradise. The Lord, Blessed and Exalted, appears to them, and they look upon Him, and musk-scented wind blows over them. They ask the Lord, Exalted, for nothing but that He gives it to them, until they return having increased in beauty and loveliness seventyfold over what they were. Then they return to their wives, and they have increased likewise."

Hisham ibn Hassan said: "Allah, Exalted and Blessed, manifests Himself to the people of Paradise, and when the people of Paradise see Him, they forget the bounties of Paradise." Tawus said: "The people of disputation and speculation will not cease to be beset by disputation and speculation until they deny the vision and oppose the people of the Sunnah." Shurayk, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, said: "The increase is looking at the face of the Most Merciful, Blessed and Exalted." Hammad ibn Zayd, from Thabit, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, that he recited this verse: ﴿For those who did good is the best (husna) and an increase﴾, and said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they are given whatever they ask for and whatever they wish. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to them: 'There remains a portion of your due that you have not been given.' Then their Lord manifests Himself to them, and then what they had been given is worth nothing at that moment. So 'the best' (al-husna) is Paradise, and 'the increase' is looking at the face of their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and no darkness nor humiliation covers their faces after their looking at their Lord, Blessed and Exalted."

Ali ibn al-Madini said: I asked Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak about the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds﴾. Abdullah said: "Whoever desires to look at the face of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, his Creator, let him do righteous deeds and tell no one of it." Nu'aym ibn Hammad said: I heard Ibn al-Mubarak say: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, never veils anyone from Himself except that He punishes him," then he recited: ﴿No! Indeed they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord. Then indeed they will burn in Hell. Then it will be said: "This is what you used to deny."﴾ He said: "By the vision." Ibn Abi al-Dunya related it from Ya'qub, from Ishaq, from Nu'aym.

Abbad ibn al-Awwam said: "Shurayk ibn Abdullah came to us fifty years ago. I said to him: 'O Abu Abdullah, there are among us people of the Mu'tazilah who deny these hadiths, that Allah descends to the lowest heaven and that the people of Paradise see their Lord. So narrate to me about ten hadiths on this.'" He said: "As for us, we took this religion of ours from the Successors, who took it from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah. So they are from whom they took it."

Uqbah ibn Qabisah said: "One day we came to Abu Nu'aym, and he came down to us from the stairway in his house, sat in its middle as if angry, and said: 'Sufyan ibn Sa'id, Mundhir al-Thawri, Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy narrated to us, and Shurayk ibn Abdullah al-Nakha'i narrated to us: these are the sons of the Emigrants narrating to us from the Messenger of Allah that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will be seen in the Hereafter, until there came a Jewish dyer's son claiming that Allah, Exalted, cannot be seen,' meaning Bishr al-Marisi."

**Section on what is transmitted from the Four Imams and their peers, their students, and those who followed their path and methods**

Mention of the statement of the Imam of the abode of emigration, Malik ibn Anas. Ahmad ibn Salih al-Misri narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Anas said: "The people will look upon their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection with their eyes." Al-Harith ibn Miskin narrated to us: Ashhab narrated to us: Malik ibn Anas was asked about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾. "Do they look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Some people say: 'It looks, but what is there to see?'" He said: "Rather, it looks at Him with a look, and Musa said: 'My Lord, show me, that I may look at You.' He said: ﴿You will not see Me﴾. And Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿No! Indeed they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.﴾"

Al-Tabari and others mention that it was said to Malik ibn Anas: "They claim that Allah cannot be seen." Malik said: "The sword, the sword!"

Mention of the statement of Ibn al-Majishun. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, said: Ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salamah al-Majishun dictated to me, and I asked him about what the Jahmiyyah denied. He said: "Satan kept whispering until they denied the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾. They said: 'No one will see Him on the Day of Resurrection,' and so they denied. By Allah, the greatest honor of Allah, with which He honors His friends on the Day of Resurrection, is looking at His face and the radiance He gives them in a seat of truth before a Sovereign, All-Powerful. By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, He will surely make the vision on the Day of Resurrection a reward for the sincere toward Him, so that their faces will be made radiant by it, apart from the wrongdoers, and their proof will prevail over the deniers. ﴿They, from their Lord that Day, will be veiled﴾, not seeing Him as they claimed that He cannot be seen, nor speaking to them, nor looking at them, and for them there is a painful punishment."

Mention of the statement of al-Awza'i. Ibn Abi Hatim related from him: "I truly hope that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will veil Jahm and his companions from the best of His reward that He promised His friends, when He says: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾. So Jahm and his companions deny the best of His reward that Allah promised His friends."

Mention of the statement of al-Layth ibn Sa'd. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Isma'il ibn Abi al-Harith narrated to us: al-Haytham ibn Kharijah narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Walid ibn Muslim say: "I asked al-Awza'i, Sufyan al-Thawri, Malik ibn Anas, and al-Layth ibn Sa'd about these hadiths in which the vision is mentioned, and they said: 'Pass them on without asking how.'"

Statement of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. Al-Tabari and others related from him that he said: "Whoever does not say that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah and that Allah is seen in Paradise is a Jahmi." Ibn Abi Hatim related from him that he said: "He prays behind the Jahmi, and the Jahmi is the one who says that his Lord is not seen on the Day of Resurrection."

Statement of Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid. Ibn Abi Hatim related from him that he mentioned the hadith of Ibn Sabit about the increase being looking at the face of Allah, and a man denied it, so he shouted at him and expelled him from his assembly.

Statement of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak. Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim related from him that a man of the Jahmiyyah said to him: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, khudaraa ba-an jahan jun bibinad," meaning: how can Allah be seen on the Day of Resurrection? He said: "With the eye."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: I heard Nu'aym ibn Hammad say: I heard Ibn al-Mubarak say: "Allah never veils anyone from Himself except that He punishes him," then he recited: ﴿No! Indeed they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord. Then indeed they will burn in Hell. Then it will be said: "This is what you used to deny."﴾ Ibn al-Mubarak said: "By the vision."

Statement of Waki' ibn al-Jarrah. Ibn Abi Hatim related from him that he said: "The believers will see Him, Blessed and Exalted, in Paradise, and none will see Him but the believers."

Statement of Qutaybah ibn Sa'id. Ibn Abi Hatim related from him that he said: "The statement of the Imams taken in Islam, the Sunnah, and the faith is belief in the vision and affirmation of the hadiths that came from the Messenger of Allah concerning the vision."

Statement of Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam. Ibn Battah and others related from him that when these hadiths about the vision were mentioned in his presence, he said: "They are true to us, and they were narrated by trustworthy narrators from trustworthy narrators until they reached us. But if we are asked to explain them to us, we say: we do not explain any of them, but we pass them on as they came."

Statement of Aswad ibn Salim, the teacher of Imam Ahmad. Al-Marwazi narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab al-Warraq narrated to us: I asked Aswad ibn Salim about the hadiths of the vision, and he said: "Swear by them, by divorce and by walking (to Mecca), that they are true."

Statement of Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i. The narration of al-Rabi' from him has already passed, that he said concerning the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿No! Indeed they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾: "Since these were veiled in wrath, this is evidence that His friends will see Him in pleasure." Al-Rabi' said: "Then, O Abu Abdullah, do we say this?" He said: "Yes, and by it..." and "if Muhammad ibn Idris were not certain that he would see Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he would not have worshipped Him." Ibn Battah said: Ibn al-Anbari narrated to us: Abu al-Qasim al-Anmati, the companion of al-Muzani, narrated to us, saying: al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: ﴿No! Indeed they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾ is evidence that the friends of Allah will see Him on the Day of Resurrection with their eyes and their faces.

Statement of the Imam of the Sunnah, Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Ishaq ibn Mansur said: "I said to Ahmad: 'Does not our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, be seen by the people of Paradise? Do you not say according to these hadiths?'" Ahmad said: "Sahih." Ibn Mansur said: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: "Sahih, and none abandons it except every innovator or weak in judgment." Al-Fadl ibn Ziyad said: "I heard Abu Abdullah, and he was asked: 'Do you say the vision?' He said: 'Whoever does not say the vision is a Jahmi.'" I heard Abu Abdullah, and it reached him that a man said: "Allah is not seen in the Hereafter," and he became extremely angry and said: "Whoever says that Allah is not seen in the Hereafter has disbelieved; upon him be the curse of Allah and His wrath, whoever he is. Does not Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾, and say: ﴿No! Indeed they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾?"

Abu Dawud said: "I heard Ahmad, and something was mentioned to him about a man concerning the vision, and he became angry and said: 'Whoever says that Allah is not seen is a disbeliever.'" Abu Dawud said: "I heard Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and he was asked about a man who narrated a hadith from a man, from Abu al-Atuf, that Allah is not seen in the Hereafter. He said: 'May Allah curse whoever narrates this hadith today,' then he said: 'May Allah disgrace this one.'"

Abu Bakr al-Marwazi said: "Abu Abdullah was asked: 'Do you know of Yazid ibn Harun, from Abu al-Atuf, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: "If the mountain remains firm, then you will see Me; if it does not remain firm, then you will not see Me, in this world or the Hereafter"?' Abu Abdullah became extremely angry, so that it showed in his face. He was sitting with people around him, so he took his sandal, put it on, and said: 'May Allah disgrace this. It should not be written down.' He denied that Yazid ibn Harun narrated it or related it, and said: 'This is a Jahmi disbeliever who opposed what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ and said: ﴿No! Indeed they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾. May Allah disgrace this wicked one.'" Abu Abdullah said: "Whoever claims that Allah is not seen in the Hereafter has disbelieved."

Abu Talib said: Abu Abdullah said: "The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, with the angels﴾ and ﴿and your Lord comes, with the angel, rank upon rank﴾. Whoever says that Allah is not seen has disbelieved."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Hani said: "I heard Abu Abdullah say: 'Whoever does not believe in the vision is a Jahmi, and the Jahmi is a disbeliever.'" Yusuf ibn Musa ibn Muhammad al-Qattan said: "It was asked of Abu Abdullah: 'Do the people of Paradise look at their Lord, Blessed and Exalted, and speak with Him, and He speaks with them?' He said: 'Yes, He looks at them, and they look at Him, and He speaks with them, and they speak with Him, however they wish, whenever they wish.'"

Hanbal ibn Ishaq said: "I heard Abu Abdullah say: 'The people return to nullification (ta'til) in their statements; they deny the vision and all the narrations. I did not think of this until I heard their statements.'" Hanbal said: "I heard Abu Abdullah say: 'Whoever claims that Allah is not seen in the Hereafter is a Jahmi, and whoever has disbelieved, and has rejected Allah and the Messenger. And whoever claims that Allah did not take Abraham as a friend has disbelieved and rejected Allah's word.'" Abu Abdullah said: "So we believe in these hadiths, affirm them, and pass them on as they came."

Al-Athram said: "I heard Abu Abdullah say: 'As for whoever says that Allah is not seen in the Hereafter, he is a Jahmi.'" Abu Abdullah said: "Only those who spoke about the vision in this world have spoken." Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Sa'igh said: "I heard Ahmad ibn Hanbal say: 'Whoever denies the vision is a zindiq (heretic).'" Hanbal said: "I heard Abu Abdullah say: 'We found the people, and they did not deny any of these hadiths, the hadiths of the vision. They used to narrate them generally, passing them on as they are, neither denying them nor doubting them.'" Abu Abdullah said: "Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or send a messenger﴾. Allah spoke to Musa from behind a veil. He said: 'My Lord, show me, that I may look at You.' He said: ﴿You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me.﴾ So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed that Musa would see Him in the Hereafter. And He said: ﴿No! Indeed they, from their Lord that Day, will be veiled﴾. There is no veil except for seeing. Allah, Exalted and Blessed, informed that whoever He wills and whoever He wishes to see Him, and the disbelievers will not see Him."

Hanbal said: "I also heard Abu Abdullah say: 'Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾, and the hadiths narrated about looking at Allah, Exalted, are the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah and others: "You will see your Lord" are sound hadiths. And He said: ﴿For those who did good is the best and an increase﴾, looking at the face of Allah, Exalted.'" Abu Abdullah said: "We believe in them and know that they are true. The hadiths of the vision: we believe that Allah is seen; we will see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection, without doubt or hesitation." He said: "And I heard Abu Abdullah say: 'Whoever claims that Allah is not seen in the Hereafter has disbelieved in Allah, denied the Qur'an, and rejected the command of Allah. He is to be asked to repent; if he repents, well; otherwise he is to be killed.'"

Hanbal said: "I asked Abu Abdullah about the hadiths of the vision, and he said: 'These are sound; we believe in them and affirm them. And whatever is narrated from the Prophet, ﷺ, with a good chain, we affirm it.'" Abu Abdullah said: "If we do not affirm what came from the Prophet, ﷺ, and reject it, and reject the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.﴾"

Statement of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. Al-Hakim, Shaykh al-Islam, and others related from him that Abdullah ibn Tahir, the governor of Khurasan, asked him: "O Abu Ya'qub, what are these hadiths that they narrate about the descent and the vision?"

He said: those who narrated the purification, the ritual bath, the prayer, and the rulings, and whatever else they mentioned, were they trustworthy in these? If not, then the rulings are abolished and the Sharia is nullified. He said: "May God heal you as you have healed me," or as he said. This is the saying of all the people of faith. Imam al-A'immah (the Imam of Imams) Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzayma said in his book: "The believers have not disagreed that the believers will see their Creator on the Day of Return, and whoever denies this is not a believer in the eyes of the believers."

The saying of al-Muzani: al-Tabari mentioned in *al-Sunnah* from Ibrahim, from Abu Dawud al-Misri, who said: "We were sitting with Nu'aym ibn Hammad when Nu'aym said to al-Muzani, 'What do you say about the Qur'an?' He said, 'I say it is the Speech of God.' He said, 'Created or uncreated?' He said, 'Uncreated.' He said, 'And do you say that God will be seen on the Day of Resurrection?' He said, 'Yes.' When the people dispersed, al-Muzani came to him and said, 'O Abu 'Abd Allah, you made me famous before the people.' He said, 'People have said much about you, so I wanted to clear you.'"

The saying of all the scholars of the Arabic language (ahl al-lughah): Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Battah said: I heard Abu 'Umar Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid, the philologist (sahib al-lughah), say: I heard Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha'lab say, concerning the saying of God Most High: ﴿And He is ever merciful to the believers. Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be peace﴾: "The scholars of the Arabic language agreed that 'meeting' here can only mean direct witnessing and seeing with the eyes."

Sufficient for you as proof of the soundness of this chain (isnad, the chain of narrators) is this; and the meeting is established by the explicit text of the Qur'an, as has preceded, and by the mass-transmitted (mutawatir, widely reported with certainty) reports from the Prophet (ﷺ). All the hadiths about the meeting are sound, such as the hadith of Anas in the story of the Well of Ma'unah: "We have met our Lord; He is pleased with us and has made us pleased."

And the hadith of 'Ubadah, 'A'ishah, Abu Hurairah and Ibn Mas'ud: "Whoever loves to meet God, God loves to meet him."

And the hadith of Anas: "You will face after me favoritism, so be patient until you meet God and His Messenger."

And the hadith of Abu Dharr: "If you come to Me with earth-full of sins, then meet Me without associating anything with Me, I will meet you with its equivalent in forgiveness."

And the hadith of Abu Musa: "Whoever meets God without associating anything with Him enters Paradise."

And other hadiths about the meeting, all of which are uniform in one wording.

(Section)

The Qur'an, the mass-transmitted Sunnah, the consensus (ijma', the agreement of scholars) of the Companions, the imams of Islam, and the people of hadith (ahl al-hadith), the core of Islam and the source of faith, and especially the Messenger of God (ﷺ), all indicate that God, glorified and exalted, will be seen on the Day of Resurrection with the eyes, directly, just as the moon is seen on the night of the full moon in clear sky, and just as the sun is seen at midday. If what God and His Messenger reported about this has a real meaning, and God has the true reality, then they can only see Him from above them, since it is impossible for them to see Him from below them, behind them, in front of them, to their right or to their left. But if what He reported has no real meaning, as the offspring of the Sabians, the philosophers, the Magians and the Pharaonists say, then the Sharia and the Qur'an are void. For the one who brought these hadiths is the one who brought the Qur'an and the Sharia, and the one who conveyed them is the one who conveyed the religion. It is not permissible that God and His Messenger should be made into ʿiḍīn (parts, [cf. ﴿those who have broken the Qur'an into parts﴾]), so that one believes in some of their meanings and disbelieves in others. Faith in the Messenger of God is not combined in the heart of a servant with knowing these hadiths, understanding their meaning, and denying them. Praise be to God who guided us to this; we would not have been guided had God not guided us. The messengers of our Lord came with the truth. Those who deviate regarding the vision of the Lord, blessed and exalted, are of two kinds:

One group claims that He is seen in this world, and that He converses and talks face to face.

The second group claims that He will not be seen in the Hereafter at all, and does not speak to His servants. What God and His Messenger reported, and what the Companions and imams agreed upon, refutes both groups. And success is from God.

The hadith of Anas about the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazid) and God's address to the people of Paradise on it many times. In general, reflect on the hadiths of the vision, and you will find that most of them mention speech. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: "Chapter: The speech of the Lord, blessed and exalted, with the people of Paradise," and included in it several hadiths. The greatest bliss of the people of Paradise is the vision of His Face, blessed and exalted, and His speaking to them. Denying that is a denial of the spirit of Paradise and the highest and most excellent of its bliss, the one with which its people are not content without. And God is the One sought for help.

**(A subtle point)**
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ (75:22–23). Thus He perfected their outward appearance with radiance, and their inner selves with gazing upon Him.

**(Another subtle point)**
If the mere sight of a created being, [Yusuf (peace be upon him)], on the day he went out before them, so overwhelmed the women's senses that they cut their hands without feeling it, then how will it be on the Day of Increase (al-Mazid)?
If you love the One worshipped, your heart will be present in His worship.

**(Section)**
Among the secrets of this surah is that Allah, glorified is He, gathered for His friends (awliya') both the beauty of the outward and the inward. He adorned their faces with radiance and their inner selves with looking upon Him. There is no greater beauty, pleasure, or sweetness for their inner selves than looking upon Him, and no greater beauty for their outward selves than the radiance of the face, which is its brightness, its embellishment, and its delight. This is like His saying in another place: ﴿And He gave them radiance and joy﴾ (76:11).

Its parallel is His saying: ﴿O Children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts, and as adornment (riyasha)﴾ (7:26). This is the beauty and adornment of the outward. Then He said: ﴿But the garment of righteousness (taqwa), that is better﴾ (7:26). This is the beauty of the inward.

Its parallel is His saying: ﴿We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars﴾ (37:6). This is the beauty of its outward. Then He said: ﴿And as a protection from every rebellious devil﴾ (37:7). This is the beauty of its inward.

Its parallel is His saying, concerning the wife of the 'Aziz after she had said to Yusuf: ﴿Go out before them.﴾ ﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him and cut their hands, and said: "Allah forbid! This is not a human. This is none but a noble angel." She said: "That is the one about whom you blamed me. I certainly sought to seduce him, but he refrained. And if he does not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned, and he will be of the debased."﴾ (12:31–32). Her mentioning him in this is part of describing his excellences, and that he was at the utmost of excellence outwardly and inwardly.

Related to this meaning, and in harmony with it, is His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is for you that you will not be hungry therein, nor will you be naked. And indeed, you will not be thirsty therein, nor will you be exposed to the sun﴾ (20:118–119). Here He contrasted hunger with nakedness, because hunger is the humiliation of the inward and nakedness is the humiliation of the outward. He also contrasted thirst, which is the heat of the inward, with exposure to the sun (ad-duha), which is the heat of the outward.

Close to this is His saying: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is taqwa﴾ (2:197), mentioning the outward sensory provision and the inward spiritual provision. The former is the provision for the journey of this world, and the latter is the provision for the journey of the Hereafter. This is connected to Hud's saying: ﴿And O my people, seek forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance; He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain and increase you in strength to your strength﴾ (11:52). The first is the outward strength, separate from them, and the second is the inward strength, joined to them.

Similar to it is His saying: ﴿So he has no strength nor any helper﴾ (86:10). Here He negated from them both the repellers: the repeller from within themselves, and the repeller from outside, which is the helper.

**(Benefit)**
In His saying: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾, it is impossible to interpret "looking" (nazar) as waiting for the reward, for He attributed the looking to the faces, which are its locus. He also made it transitive with the particle ilā (toward), which, when the verb of seeing is joined to it, means only the seeing of the eye. He described the faces with radiance, which is attained only with the presence of what is enjoyed, not with the distress of awaiting it. With this construction it is also impossible to interpret "looking" as other than sight, although "nazar" in the sense of "waiting" has been used in His saying: ﴿Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light﴾ (57:13), and His saying: ﴿And I will wait (nathira) with what the messengers will return﴾ (27:35).

He also said in *al-Sawa'iq al-Mursala*: Similar to this is the consistent manner of the texts regarding looking at Allah: "Thus you will see your Lord, and you will look upon your Lord," and ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾. It has never come in a single place "you will see the reward of your Lord," so that what departs from its counterparts would be interpreted in that way.

**[Section: The perfection of pleasure is in the perfection of the Beloved and the perfection of love]**
This is a great matter which the intelligent person must attend to: that the perfection of pleasure, joy, delight, the bliss of the heart, and the gladness of the spirit follows two matters. The first is the perfection of the Beloved in Himself and in His beauty, and that He is most deserving of having love directed to Him above everything else. The second matter is the perfection of one's love, the exhausting of one's effort in loving Him, and preferring nearness to Him and reaching Him above all things.

Every intelligent person knows that the pleasure of attaining the Beloved is in proportion to the strength of one's love. Whenever love is stronger, the lover's pleasure is more complete. So the servant's pleasure is in proportion to the intensity of his thirst upon attaining cool water, or the intensity of his hunger upon eating delicious food, and similar things, according to the measure of his longing and the intensity of his will and love.

Once you know this, pleasure, delight, and joy are matters sought in themselves; indeed they are the aim of every living and intelligent being. When pleasure is sought for its own sake, it is blamed if it results in a greater pain, or if it prevents a better and more lasting pleasure. How much more so if it results in the greatest regrets and causes the loss of the greatest delights and joys? It is praised when it helps toward a great, lasting, firmly established pleasure, in which there is no distress or turbidity in any way, and that is the pleasure of the Hereafter, its bliss, and the goodness of life therein. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ (87:16–17).

When the sorcerers said to Pharaoh after they had believed: ﴿So decide what you will decide. You can only decide concerning this worldly life. Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and the magic you compelled us to practice. And Allah is better and more enduring﴾ (20:72–73).

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, created the creation so that He might bestow upon them this lasting pleasure in the abode of eternity. As for this world, it is cut off, and its pleasures never become pure nor do they endure. This is unlike the Hereafter, whose pleasures are lasting, and whose bliss is pure of every turbidity and pain. In it is what the souls desire and what the eyes delight in, along with eternity forever. ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes﴾ (32:17). Rather, in it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human.

This is the meaning intended by the sincere advisor to his people: ﴿O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the path of right conduct. O my people, indeed this worldly life is but enjoyment, and indeed the Hereafter is the abode of permanence﴾ (40:38–39). He informed them that this world is enjoyed as a means to something else, and that the Hereafter is the place of settling.

Once you know that the pleasures and bliss of this world are an enjoyment and a means to the pleasures of the Hereafter, and that for this reason this world and its pleasures were created, then every pleasure that helped toward the pleasure of the Hereafter and led to it is not blamed for being taken. Rather, it is praised according to the extent to which it leads to the pleasure of the Hereafter.

Once this is known, the greatest bliss and pleasures of the Hereafter are: looking upon the Face of the Lord, may His majesty be exalted; hearing His speech directly from Him; and nearness to Him. As is established in the Sahih in the hadith of the vision: "By Allah, He has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking upon Him." And in another hadith: "When He manifests Himself to them and they see Him, they forget what they are in of bliss."

In the Sunan of al-Nasa'i and the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) in his supplication: "And I ask You, O Allah, for the delight of looking upon Your Noble Face, and the longing for meeting You." In *Kitab al-Sunnah* of 'Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad, marfu' (traced to the Prophet): "It is as if people on the Day of Resurrection had never heard the Qur'an, when they hear it from the Most Merciful, as if they had not heard it before that."

**[Section: That the delight of looking upon the Face of Allah on the Day of Resurrection follows the enjoyment of knowing and loving Him in this world]**
Just as there is no comparison between the bliss of anything in Paradise and the bliss of looking upon the Face of the Most High, glorified is He, so there is no comparison between the bliss of this world and the bliss of loving Him, knowing Him, longing for Him, and being intimate with Him. Rather, the delight of looking upon Him, glorified is He, follows their knowledge of Him and their love for Him, for pleasure follows perception and love. Thus, whenever the lover is more knowing of the Beloved and more intense in love for Him, his delight in His nearness, his vision, and his arrival to Him will be greater.

**(Section)**
Hisham ibn Hassan said, from al-Hasan (al-Basri): When the people of Paradise look upon Allah, Exalted is He, they forget the bliss of Paradise.

Hisham ibn 'Ammar said: Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Sabur narrated to us; 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman narrated to us; Sa'id ibn 'Abd Allah al-Jarshi al-Qadi narrated to us, that he heard Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani narrate from al-Harith al-A'war, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, traced to the Prophet, who said:

"When Allah has settled the people of Paradise in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire, He will send to the people of Paradise the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibril), who will say: 'O people of Paradise, indeed your Lord sends you His greetings and commands you to visit Him at the courtyard of Paradise, which is its open plain (abtah), whose soil is musk, whose pebbles are pearls and rubies, whose trees are of gold with fresh fruit, and whose leaves are emerald.' So the people of Paradise go forth joyful and glad. Then He gathers them there, and there is the honor of Allah and the looking upon His Face, which is the promise of Allah that He has fulfilled for them. Allah then permits them to listen, eat, and drink, and they are clothed in garments of honor. Then a caller calls: 'O friends of Allah, has there remained anything of what Allah your Lord promised you?' They say: 'No. We have received what was promised to us, and nothing remains except looking upon His Face.' Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, manifests Himself to them behind veils and says: 'O Jibril, raise My veil for My servants, that they may look upon My Face.'

He said: So the first veil is raised, and they look upon a light from the light of the Lord, and they fall down prostrate before Him. The Lord calls to them: 'O My servants, raise your heads, for this is not an abode of works; it is only an abode of reward.' Then the second veil is raised, and they look upon something even greater and more majestic, so they fall prostrate in praise of Allah. The Lord calls to them: 'Raise your heads, for this is not an abode of works; it is only an abode of reward and lasting bliss.' Then the third veil is raised, and at that moment they look upon the Face of the Lord of the worlds. They say, when they look upon His Face: 'Glory be to You; we have not worshipped You with the worship You deserve.'

Then He says: 'My honor has enabled you to look upon My Face and has made you dwell in My abode.' Allah then permits Paradise to speak, and it says: 'Blessed is the one who dwells in me, blessed is the one who lives forever in me, blessed is the one for whom I have been prepared.' This is His saying: ﴿Blessed are they, and a good return﴾ (13:29), and His saying: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾."

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There are two gardens of gold, their vessels and ornaments and what is in them; and two gardens of silver, their vessels and ornaments and what is in them. Nothing stands between the people and looking upon their Lord except the cloak of greatness over His Face in the Garden of Eden."

'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi narrated: Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us; Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ka'b (al-Ahbar), who said: Allah has never looked upon Paradise except that He said: "Be good for your people," and it increased in goodness beyond what it was. And there is no day that was a festival in this world except that they go out, in its measure, to the gardens of Paradise, and the Lord, blessed and exalted, manifests Himself to them and they look upon Him, and the wind blows upon them with perfume and musk. They ask their Lord, blessed and exalted, for nothing except that He gives it to them. Then they return to their families, having increased in beauty and goodliness seventy times over what they had been.

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Shababah informed me, from Isra'il, who narrated to us, from Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks upon his servants, his bliss, and his couches for a distance of a thousand years; and the most honored of them before Allah is the one who looks upon His Face morning and evening." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾. Related by al-Tirmidhi in his *Jami'*, from him.

'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi narrated from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When the people of Paradise reach the fullest extent of bliss and think there is no bliss greater than it, the Lord, blessed and exalted, manifests Himself to them, and they look upon the Face of the Most Merciful, and they forget every bliss they had witnessed when they looked upon the Face of the Most Merciful."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding His saying: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾: "Allah has beautified them by looking upon Him, glorified is He, and it is rightful for them to be radiant while looking upon their Lord, Mighty and Majestic."

Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: "If the people of love, or he said the people of knowledge (ma'rifah), had nothing but this verse, ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾, it would suffice them."

al-Nasa'i mentioned, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Do you suffer any difficulty in seeing the sun on a day with no clouds, and the moon on a full-moon night with no haze?" We said: "No." He said: "Indeed you will see your Lord, until one of you will be brought near to Him, and He will say: 'My servant, do you recognize such-and-such a sin?' He will say: 'O Lord, did You not forgive me?' He will say: 'By My forgiveness you have reached this.'"

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, says to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise!' They say: 'At your service, our Lord, and at your pleasure, and all good is in Your hands.' He says: 'Are you content?' They say: 'And why would we not be content, when You have given us what You have not given anyone of Your creation?' He says: 'Shall I not give you something better than that?' They say: 'O Lord, and what is better than that?' He says: 'I shall let My pleasure descend upon you, and I shall never be displeased with you after this.'"

In the Sahih, the Sunan, and the Masanid, from the hadith of Thabit al-Bunani, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, a caller calls: 'O people of Paradise! Indeed you have a promise with Allah, which He wishes to fulfill for you.' They say: 'What is it? Has He not whitened our faces, made heavy our scales, admitted us to Paradise, and saved us from the Fire?' Then the veil is lifted, and they look upon Him. By Allah, Allah has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking upon Him, nor anything more pleasing to their eyes."

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: "Indeed you will see your Lord as you see this moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in performing the prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so."

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Ata' ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that people said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you have any difficulty seeing the moon on the night of the full moon?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Do you have any difficulty seeing the sun when there is no cloud between us and it?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Indeed you will see Him in the same way." And in another wording: "Indeed you will not be harmed in seeing your Lord except as you are harmed in seeing them both."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 75, verses 22–23 (part 2 of 7):

Al-Tirmidhi said: Qutaybah narrated to us: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection in one plain. Then the Lord of the worlds, blessed and exalted, will look down upon them and say: 'Let every person follow what he used to worship.' So the one who worshipped the cross will be given his cross, the one who worshipped images will be given his images, and the one who worshipped the fire will be given his fire, and they will follow what they used to worship. The Muslims will remain, and the Lord of the worlds, blessed and exalted, will look down upon them and say: 'Will you not follow the people?' They will say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from You, we seek refuge in Allah from You. Allah is our Lord. This is our place until we see our Lord.' And He will command them and make them firm. Then He will withdraw, and then He will look down upon them again and say: 'Will you not follow the people?' They will say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from You, we seek refuge in Allah from You. Allah is our Lord, and this is our place until we see our Lord.' And He will command them and make them firm." They said: "Will we see Him, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Do you have any difficulty seeing the moon on the night of the full moon?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Then you will have no difficulty seeing Him at that hour." He said: "Then He will withdraw, and then He will look down and make Himself known to them, and then He will say: 'I am your Lord, so follow Me.' The Muslims will stand up, and the Ṣirāṭ (bridge) will be set up, and they will cross over it like the swiftest horses and riders, and their saying on it will be: 'Safety, safety!' The people of the Fire will remain, and a group of them will be cast into it. It will be said: 'Are you full?' and it will say: 'Is there more?' Then another group will be cast into it, and it will be said: 'Are you full?' and it will say: 'Is there more?' until, when they have been fully filled, the Most Merciful, blessed and exalted, will place His foot in it, and it will draw in upon itself, and say: 'Qaṭ, qaṭ (Enough, enough).' Then when Allah has admitted the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of the Fire into the Fire, Death will be brought in a form (mulabbiyan) and stopped on the wall between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. Then it will be said: 'O people of Paradise!' and they will look up in fear. Then it will be said: 'O people of the Fire!' and they will look up rejoicing, hoping for intercession. It will be said to the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire: 'Do you recognize this?' They will say: 'Yes, both of us recognize it. It is Death, which was assigned to us.' Then it will be laid down and slaughtered at the wall. Then it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, eternal life with no death! O people of the Fire, eternal life with no death!'"

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hadith ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ (good and sound). Its origin is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim), but this wording is more comprehensive and more concise. In the wording of al-Tirmidhi: "If anyone were to die from joy, the people of Paradise would die, and if anyone were to die from grief, the people of the Fire would die."

In the Musnad of al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Usāmah, from the narration of Qurrah, from Mālik, from Ziyād ibn Saʿd, who said: Abū al-Zubayr narrated to us, saying: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh (may Allah be pleased with both of them) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the nations will be gathered, and every people will be called with their leader. We will come last among the people, and someone among the people will say: 'Is this from this Ummah?' Then the people will look towards us, and it will be said: 'This is the trustworthy nation, this is the Ummah of Muhammad, and this is Muhammad among his Ummah.' Then a caller will call out: 'You are the last and the first.' So we will come and step over the necks of the people until we are the closest of the people to Allah, the Exalted, in station. Then the people will be called, each people with their leader. The Jews will be called, and it will be said: 'Who are you?' They will say: 'We are the Jews.' It will be said: 'Who is your prophet?' They will say: 'Our prophet is Mūsā (Moses).' It will be said: 'What is your book?' They will say: 'Our book is the Torah.' It will be said: 'What do you worship?' They will say: 'We worship ʿUzayr and we worship Allah.' He will say to those around Him: 'Lead them into Hell.' Then the Christians will be called, and it will be said: 'Who are you?' They will say: 'We are the Christians.' It will be said: 'Who is your prophet?' They will say: 'Our prophet is ʿĪsā (Jesus).' It will be said: 'What is your book?' They will say: 'Our book is the Gospel.' It will be said: 'What do you worship?' They will say: 'We worship ʿĪsā and his mother, and Allah.' He will say to those around Him: 'Lead these into Hell.' Then ʿĪsā will be called, and He will say to ʿĪsā: 'O ʿĪsā, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?' He will say: 'Glory be to You, it is not for me to say what I have no right to say,' up to His words ﴿the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾.

Then every people will be called with what they used to worship. Then a crier will cry out: 'O people, whoever used to worship a god, let him follow it.' Their gods will go before them, some of them wood and stones, some the sun and the moon, and some the Dajjāl (Antichrist), until only the Muslims remain. He will stand over them and say: 'Who are you?' They will say: 'We are the Muslims.' He said: 'The best name and the best call.' He will say: 'Who is your prophet?' They will say: 'Muhammad.' He will say: 'What is your book?' They will say: 'The Qur'ān.' He will say: 'What do you worship?' They will say: 'We worship Allah alone, with no partner.' He said: 'That will benefit you, if you are sincere.' They said: 'This is our day that we were promised.' He will say: 'Do you know Allah when you see Him?' They will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'And how do you know Him when you have not seen Him?' They will say: 'We know that there is none like Him.' He said: 'Then He will reveal Himself to them, blessed and exalted, and they will say: "You are our Lord, blessed are Your names," and they will prostrate to Him. Then the light will pass on with its people."

In the Musnad of Imam Aḥmad (may Allah be pleased with him), from the narration of Abū al-Zubayr, who said: I asked Jābir about the approach (al-wurūd), and he informed me that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "We will come on the Day of Resurrection to a mound above the people, and the nations will be called with their idols and what they used to worship, the first and then the next. Then our Lord will come to us after that and say: 'What are you waiting for?' They will say: 'We are waiting for our Lord.' He will say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'Until we look at You.' Then He will reveal Himself to them, laughing, and they will follow Him."

ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī mentioned that Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā al-Ashʿarī came to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and said: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will gather the nations on the Day of Resurrection in one plain. When He wishes to separate His creation, He will make a likeness for every people of what they used to worship, and they will follow them until they cast them into the Fire. Then our Lord will come to us while we are in a place, and He will say: 'Who are you?' We will say: 'We are the believers.' He will say: 'What are you waiting for?' We will say: 'We are waiting for our Lord.' He will say: 'How do you know that He is your Lord?' We will say: 'The messengers told us, or the books came to us.' He will say: 'Do you know Him?' They will say: 'We know that there is none like Him.' Then He will reveal Himself to us laughing, and He will say: 'Rejoice, O Muslims, for there is not one of you but that a Jew or a Christian has been put in his place in the Fire.'"

ʿUmar said to Abū Burdah: "By Allah, did you hear Abū Mūsā narrate this hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, besides whom there is no god, I heard my father mention it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) more than once, not twice or three times." ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: "I have not heard in Islam a hadith more beloved to me than this one."

In al-Tirmidhi, from the narration of al-Awzāʿī, who said: Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyyah narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, that he met Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), and Abū Hurayrah said: "I ask Allah, exalted, to gather me and you in the market of Paradise." Saʿīd said: "Is there a market in it?" He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed me that when the people of Paradise enter it, they will descend according to the merit of their deeds. They will be permitted to stay for a period equal to a Friday of worldly days, and they will visit Allah, blessed and exalted. His Throne will be displayed to them, and He will manifest Himself to them in a garden of the gardens of Paradise. Pulpits of light, pulpits of pearls, pulpits of ruby, pulpits of chrysolite, pulpits of gold and pulpits of silver will be set up for them. The lowest of them, and there is no one lowly among them, will sit on mounds of musk and camphor. They will not think that those on the chairs are superior to them in station."
